The reader is told the final section covers random errors (false — it covers arbitrary/continuous errors, the central QEC point that discrete corrections handle any error), and the deliberate random-vs-arbitrary distinction is erased entirely. Secondary, non-misleading issues: "anti-commute" is flattened to "يتعاكسان" ("they are opposite") instead of an anti-commutation rendering such as "يتبادلان التبديل تضاداً"; "It follows that / follows from the fact that" is calqued three times in a row as "يتبع أن … من كون …" (lines 167, 169, 171), which no Arabic technical writer would use in place of "يترتب على ذلك أن / ويعود ذلك إلى أن"; and there are number/agreement slips ("ثلاثة كتل" for "ثلاث كتل" line 23, "أثّر خطأُي X وZ" line 124, "بشكل مستقل تاماً" line 122). Register is correctly informal ("دعنا نتأمل") and core terms (كيوبت، بوابة، متلازمة، الشيفرة الداخلية/الخارجية، الانحطاط) are correct and consistent.

examples.source: Before we move on to the last section of the lesson, which concerns arbitrary quantum errors, let's briefly consider the performance of the 9-qubit Shor code when errors represented by Pauli matrices occur *randomly* on the qubits.
examples.suggested: قبل الانتقال إلى القسم الأخير من الدرس المتعلق بالأخطاء الكمومية الاعتباطية (الكيفية)، دعنا نتأمل بإيجاز أداء شيفرة شور ذات 9 كيوبتات عندما تقع أخطاء ممثَّلة بمصفوفات باولي *بشكل عشوائي* على الكيوبتات.
examples.translation: قبل الانتقال إلى القسم الأخير من الدرس المتعلق بالأخطاء الكمومية العشوائية، دعنا نتأمل بإيجاز أداء شيفرة شور ذات 9 كيوبتات عندما تقع أخطاء ممثَّلة بمصفوفات باولي *بشكل عشوائي* على الكيوبتات.
examples.why: 'arbitrary' is rendered as 'عشوائية' (random) — the same word used later in the sentence for 'randomly'. The learner is told the final section is about random errors (it is about arbitrary/continuous errors) and the random-vs-arbitrary contrast that motivates the rest of the lesson disappears; the sentence also reads as self-contradictory since this very section is the random-error one.

examples.source: To be clear, $X$ and $Z$ do not commute, they *anti-commute*:
examples.suggested: وللتوضيح، $X$ و$Z$ لا يتبادلان التبديل، بل *يتبادلان التبديل تضاداً* (تعاكسًا في التبديل):
examples.translation: وللتوضيح، $X$ و$Z$ لا يتبادلان التبديل، بل يتعاكسان:
examples.why: 'يتعاكسان' means merely 'they are opposite/inverse of each other' and does not name anti-commutation; the italicized technical term is lost. The equation that follows rescues the meaning, so this is recognizable but imprecise.

examples.source: The fact that this procedure works as expected, even in the presence of one or more $X$ errors, follows from the fact that $X$ gates on any of the nine qubits used for the encoding commute with all of the gates in our simplified circuit...
examples.suggested: ويعود عمل هذا الإجراء كما هو متوقع، حتى في وجود خطأ $X$ أو أكثر، إلى أن بوابات $X$ على أي من الكيوبتات التسعة المستخدمة للترميز تتبادل التبديل مع جميع البوابات...
examples.translation: يتبع أن هذا الإجراء يعمل كما هو متوقع، حتى في وجود خطأ $X$ أو أكثر، من كون بوابات $X$ على أي من الكيوبتات التسعة المستخدمة للترميز تتبادل التبديل مع جميع البوابات...
examples.why: 'يتبع أن … من كون …' is a word-for-word calque of 'follows from the fact that' with the subject clause stranded; it recurs three times in a row (lines 167, 169, 171) and reads as machine syntax rather than Arabic technical prose.

examples.source: just like the 3-bit repetition code is worse than no code when $p$ is larger than one-half.
examples.suggested: تماماً كما أن شيفرة التكرار الثلاثي تكون أسوأ من عدم استخدام أي شيفرة عندما يكون $p$ أكبر من النصف.
examples.translation: تماماً كشيفرة التكرار الثلاثي التي تكون أسوأ من لا شيفرة عندما يكون $p$ أكبر من النصف.
examples.why: 'أسوأ من لا شيفرة' is an ungrammatical literal transfer of 'worse than no code'; meaning survives but no native technical writer would write it.

editor_note: The prose is fluent, natural Spanish and the physics is faithful throughout the mathematical sections (spectral decomposition, the λ0 lower-bound derivation, the equality condition |ψ(θ*)⟩ = |φ0⟩ are all rendered exactly). Two things a native technical editor would change. (1) Within-file term split: the section headings say "Teorema variacional" / "Teorema variacional de la mecánica cuántica", but every body mention renders "variational theorem" as "principio variacional" (line 64 "el _principio variacional_ de la mecánica cuántica", line 129 "La razón por la que el principio variacional se formula en términos de mínimos de energía"); theorem and principle are distinct labels in Spanish physics writing and the reader is bounced between them. (2) Opening claim shifted: EN "This course covers the specifics of variational algorithms" became "Este curso cubre los fundamentos de los algoritmos variacionales" — "the specifics" (the details of each step) is not "los fundamentos" (the basics), which understates what the course promises. Neither would make a learner form a false belief about the physics, so both stay MINOR. Register is correctly informal tú ("puedes profundizar", "has obtenido", "completa esta breve encuesta").

examples.source: A key insight we'll use is the _variational theorem_ of quantum mechanics. / The reason why the variational theorem is stated in terms of energy minima...
examples.suggested: Una idea central que utilizaremos es el _teorema variacional_ de la mecánica cuántica. / La razón por la que el teorema variacional se formula en términos de mínimos de energía...
examples.translation: Una idea central que utilizaremos es el _principio variacional_ de la mecánica cuántica. / La razón por la que el principio variacional se formula en términos de mínimos de energía...
examples.why: The headings ('Teorema variacional', 'Teorema variacional de la mecánica cuántica') and the body ('principio variacional') use two different names for the same object. In Spanish physics usage 'principio variacional' and 'teorema variacional' are not interchangeable labels, so the reader cannot tell whether the section is about the thing the headings announced.

examples.source: This course covers the specifics of variational algorithms and near-term hybrid quantum-classical algorithms based on the variational theorem of quantum mechanics.
examples.suggested: Este curso aborda en detalle los algoritmos variacionales y los algoritmos híbridos cuántico-clásicos de corto plazo, basados en el teorema variacional de la mecánica cuántica.
examples.translation: Este curso cubre los fundamentos de los algoritmos variacionales y los algoritmos híbridos cuántico-clásicos a corto plazo, basados en el principio variacional de la mecánica cuántica.
examples.why: 'the specifics' (the concrete details of each design step, which is exactly what the following lessons deliver) is weakened to 'los fundamentos' (the basics), softening what the course claims to cover. Secondary nit in the same sentence: 'a corto plazo' is a calque of 'near-term'; 'de corto plazo' reads better attributively.

editor_note: No misleading content: the whole physics chain (QUBO cost Hamiltonian, tetrahedral-lattice turn encoding, the (-1)^k A/B-site cancellation argument, Jordan-Wigner relations, Schwinger-model Hamiltonian) is faithful, and the informal "tú" register holds throughout ("Mira el video", "quizás recuerdes", "Usa la función"). What a native technical editor would still change: the fermionic operators are consistently rendered "operadores de creación y destrucción" (lines ~139, 156, 180, 181, 185) where the settled Spanish convention is "creación y aniquilación" — recognizable, but non-standard for a physics text. "Pero a este punto hemos hablado..." (line 45) is a calque of "at this point" (native: "llegados a este punto" / "a estas alturas"), and "core (non-interacting) orbitals" becomes "orbitales centrales" (line 181) instead of the usual "orbitales internos/de core". Two small qualifiers are dropped: "even in the 100-qubit, utility-scale example" loses "incluso" (line 55) and "among other options" disappears from the bosonic-transformation sentence (line 143). None of these change the meaning a learner takes away.

examples.source: These are basically mathematical objects that correspond to creating or annihilating a fermion from a state in the system.
examples.suggested: ...que corresponden a crear o aniquilar un fermión...; y "operadores de creación y aniquilación" en el resto del archivo
examples.translation: Estos son básicamente objetos matemáticos que corresponden a crear o destruir un fermión de un estado en el sistema.
examples.why: The Spanish physics convention is "operadores de creación y aniquilación"; "destrucción/destruir" is used consistently here but is not the field term. Recognizable, so MINOR, not misleading.

examples.source: But at this point we have spoken abstractly enough about the challenge before us.
examples.suggested: Pero, llegados a este punto, ya hemos hablado bastante en abstracto sobre el desafío que tenemos por delante.
examples.translation: Pero a este punto hemos hablado de manera suficientemente abstracta sobre el desafío que tenemos por delante.
examples.why: "a este punto" is a direct calque of "at this point"; a native technical writer would use "llegados a este punto" or "a estas alturas".

examples.source: the creation of an identity matrix which represents the core (non-interacting) orbitals
examples.suggested: ...que represente los orbitales internos (de core, no interactuantes)
examples.translation: crear una matriz identidad que represente los orbitales centrales (no interactuantes)
examples.why: "core orbitals" in quantum chemistry are "orbitales internos" (or "de core"); "orbitales centrales" reads as a literal rendering and could momentarily confuse a chemistry-trained reader, though the parenthetical rescues it.

examples.source: In that lesson, even in the 100-qubit, utility-scale example, the graph connectivity already matched the topology... / ...to a sub-basis of the available bosonic modes, among other options.
examples.suggested: En esa lección, incluso en el ejemplo de 100 qubits a escala de utilidad, la conectividad... / ...de los modos bosónicos disponibles, entre otras opciones.
examples.translation: En esa lección, la conectividad del grafo en el ejemplo de 100 qubits a escala de utilidad ya coincidía con la topología... / ...a una subbasis de los modos bosónicos disponibles.
examples.why: Two small qualifiers dropped: the emphatic "even" (which carries the point that the match held even at utility scale) and "among other options". Neither changes the claim, so MINOR.

editor_note: No semantic drift or hallucination found: every substantive claim tracks the English, including the delicate ones (Module-LWE "más eficiencia que LWE (aunque menos que Ring-LWE)... mayor garantía de seguridad que Ring-LWE", the LWE decryption condition, "IND-CCA es una noción de seguridad más fuerte que IND-CPA y la subsume", and the hybrid-crypto "al menos no menos segura", which even repairs a broken English sentence). Core terminology is correct and consistent (lattice→retículo everywhere, SVP→problema del vector más corto, CVP→problema del vector más cercano, KEM→mecanismo de encapsulación de clave, decapsulation→desencapsulación, plaintext→texto en claro, ciphertext→texto cifrado), and the informal "tú" register holds ("Imagina que tienes...", "Consulta los enlaces...", "puedas ver la distribución"). What a native technical editor would still change: "quantum-resistant" rendered as "resistente al Cuanto"/"resistente al cuanto" (an odd calque; the field says "resistente a lo cuántico" or "cuántico-resistente"), "quantum speedups" flattened to "las ventajas cuánticas" (speedup ≠ advantage; "aceleraciones cuánticas"), "Python language binding" as "el enlace del lenguaje Python" (reads as "link", especially sitting next to a URL — "vínculo/binding de lenguaje"), plus small agreement/register slips: "primitivos criptográficos" (should be "primitivas criptográficas"), "problemas NP-completo", and the colloquial "crackeado" for "cracked".

examples.source: This is also sometimes called **quantum-resistant**, or **post-quantum cryptography**.
examples.suggested: Esto también se denomina a veces **cuántico-resistente** (o **resistente a lo cuántico**), o **criptografía poscuántica**.
examples.translation: Esto también se denomina a veces **resistente al cuanto**, o **criptografía poscuántica**.
examples.why: "Resistente al cuanto" is a literal calque; "el cuanto" (the quantum, as a particle) is not what is being resisted — attacks by quantum computers are. Same wording appears in the DefinitionTooltip ("También conocida como Post-Cuántica o Resistente al Cuanto"). Recognizable, so MINOR, but no Spanish cryptographer would write it.

examples.source: ...where the quantum speedups are not super-polynomial.
examples.suggested: ...donde las aceleraciones cuánticas no son superpolinómicas.
examples.translation: ...donde las ventajas cuánticas no son super-polinomiales.
examples.why: "Speedup" is a quantified ratio (aceleración), not a generic "ventaja". The paragraph's whole point is the size of the speedup for Grover/BHT vs Shor, so the precise term matters pedagogically; "ventaja cuántica" additionally collides with the loaded term for quantum advantage.

examples.source: **Python Library:** This provides the Python language binding for liboqs - https://github.com/...
examples.suggested: **Biblioteca Python:** Proporciona el binding (vínculo de lenguaje) de Python para liboqs - ...
examples.translation: **Biblioteca Python:** Proporciona el enlace del lenguaje Python para liboqs - https://github.com/...
examples.why: "Binding" rendered as "enlace" is the wrong sense of the word, and because a URL follows on the same line the reader is likely to parse "enlace" as "hyperlink" rather than "language binding".

examples.source: ...traditional cryptographic primitives... / based on NP-complete problems... / was subsequently cracked and proven to be insecure.
examples.suggested: ...primitivas criptográficas tradicionales... / problemas NP-completos... / fue posteriormente vulnerado (roto) y demostrado inseguro.
examples.translation: ...primitivos criptográficos tradicionales... / se basan en problemas NP-completo... / fue posteriormente crackeado y demostrado inseguro.
examples.why: Three small native-editor fixes: "primitiva criptográfica" is feminine in Spanish crypto usage; "NP-completo" needs plural agreement with "problemas"; and "crackeado" is a colloquial anglicism out of register for a NIST-standardization paragraph.

editor_note: Three substantive defects. (1) A whole EN paragraph is missing: after the first "Train accuracy: 60.0%" output the English says "The training accuracy is only 60%, which is definitely not good. It is hard to imagine that the model's performance on the test set could be any better. Let's verify." — the FR file jumps straight from the output block to the next ```python cell, so the learner loses the verdict on the 60% figure and the set-up for the test run. (2) The naming-convention sentence is corrupted: EN "we are adopting 'qnn' in some of our naming conventions" became « nous adoptons « rnn » dans certaines de nos conventions de nommage » — the code in this very lesson uses qnn_circuit / qnn_cnot_list, and "RNN" is an established, different ML concept (recurrent neural network). (3) "two-qubit depth" is rendered as « profondeur de deux qubits », which in « C'est une profondeur raisonnable de deux qubits » parses as "a reasonable depth of two qubits" and contradicts the printed "2+ qubit depth: 5"; the file elsewhere renders the same concept correctly as « profondeur de portes à deux qubits », so the term is also split within the file. Secondary: "shallowest circuit" is consistently « le plus superficiel » (should be « le moins profond »), "unseen images" became « images invisibles », "entangle" appears once as « entrelacer » against « intrication » elsewhere, and there are calques (« En mappeant », « Nous voulons aussi savoir sur les lignes verticales », « la profondeur ici est fine », « Monitorer la profondeur »).

examples.source: The training accuracy is only $60%$, which is definitely not good. It is hard to imagine that the model's performance on the test set could be any better. Let's verify.
examples.suggested: La précision d'entraînement n'est que de 60 %, ce qui n'est franchement pas bon. On imagine mal que les performances du modèle sur l'ensemble de test soient meilleures. Vérifions-le.
examples.translation: (entire paragraph absent — FR goes from the ```text output block straight to the next ```python cell)
examples.why: A full paragraph of source content is dropped. The learner is shown the 60% figure with no evaluation of it and no set-up for the test-set run that immediately follows, so the pedagogical thread (bad result → check the test set → diagnose) is broken.

examples.source: Since this analogy holds in this case, we are adopting "qnn" in some of our naming conventions; but this analogy should not be limiting in your exploration of VQCs.
examples.suggested: … nous adoptons « qnn » dans certaines de nos conventions de nommage ; …
examples.translation: Puisque cette analogie tient dans ce cas, nous adoptons « rnn » dans certaines de nos conventions de nommage ; mais cette analogie ne doit pas limiter ton exploration des VQC.
examples.why: The sentence describes the identifiers actually used in this lesson's code (qnn_circuit, qnn_cnot_list, "# QNN ansatz"). Writing « rnn » makes the statement false about the file's own code and points at RNN (réseau de neurones récurrent), a different architecture — a false concept for a reader of an ML course.

examples.source: This is a reasonable two-qubit depth. We should be able to get high-quality results from a real quantum computer.
examples.suggested: C'est une profondeur en portes à deux qubits raisonnable. Nous devrions pouvoir obtenir des résultats de haute qualité sur un vrai ordinateur quantique.
examples.translation: C'est une profondeur raisonnable de deux qubits. Nous devrions pouvoir obtenir des résultats de haute qualité d'un vrai ordinateur quantique.
examples.why: With that word order the French reads "a reasonable depth of two qubits", i.e. a depth equal to 2 — while the cell just above prints "2+ qubit depth: 5". It states a quantity the English does not and mis-teaches what two-qubit depth means. The same concept is rendered correctly as « profondeur de portes à deux qubits » earlier in the file (Hardware bullet), so the term is also inconsistent.

examples.source: …run such pass managers several times and use the best circuit / use the best (shallowest) result / select the shallowest circuit
examples.suggested: …le circuit le moins profond / le meilleur résultat (celui de plus faible profondeur) / sélectionner le circuit de plus faible profondeur
examples.translation: …le circuit le plus efficace et le plus superficiel / d'utiliser le meilleur (le plus superficiel) résultat / sélectionner le circuit le plus superficiel
examples.why: « superficiel » in French means shallow in the figurative sense (superficial); circuit depth takes « profondeur », so the antonym is « peu profond / de faible profondeur ». Recognizable but not what a French quantum engineer would write, and it is used four times.

examples.source: In mapping our problem to a quantum circuit, we should have explicitly thought about … We also want to know about vertical lines.
examples.suggested: En mappant notre problème sur un circuit quantique, … Nous voulons aussi détecter les lignes verticales.
examples.translation: En mappeant notre problème à un circuit quantique, nous aurions dû penser explicitement à … Nous voulons aussi savoir sur les lignes verticales.
examples.why: « En mappeant » is a malformed gerund (« en mappant »), and « savoir sur les lignes verticales » is a word-for-word calque of "know about" that is ungrammatical in French. Same paragraph later has « la profondeur ici est fine » (anglicism for "is fine"; « convient »).

examples.source: our goal is to label unseen images into one of the two categories
examples.suggested: notre objectif est de classer des images inédites (jamais vues) dans l'une des deux catégories
examples.translation: notre objectif est de classer les images invisibles dans l'une des deux catégories
examples.why: "Unseen" here means "not seen during training", a standard ML notion; « invisibles » is a false friend meaning "that cannot be seen", which makes no sense for images that are then plotted and classified.

editor_note: No semantic drift or hallucination: the two correction tables (téléportation « 01 »→porte X / « 10 »→porte Z, and superdense 01→porte Z / 10→porte X) are faithful, the little-endian/100 % paragraph, the "communication classique _était_ disponible" contrast, and the two takeaway Q&A ("plus vite que la lumière", non-clonage) all match the English exactly. Remaining defects are editorial only: "mapping" (the Qiskit-patterns step) is rendered "cartographie" while the sibling heading says "Mapper le problème" — an imperfect and internally inconsistent rendering; "trace out Bob's results" becomes "tu peux tracer les résultats de Bob", which a French reader parses as "plot", not as marginalisation/trace partielle. Two register/grammar slips: "Supposons qu'ils ne peuvent communiquer" (needs subjunctive "puissent") and the infinitive "(Consulter la [porte U]…)" where the file's tu-convention elsewhere gives "consulte [la référence API]". Terminology is otherwise correct and consistent (qubit, e-bit, intrication, base computationnelle, matrice densité, porte, backend, primitive Runtime Sampler, transpilation, carte de couplage).

examples.source: Or, using `marginal_count`, you can trace out Bob's results on qubit 2.
examples.suggested: …tu peux isoler (par marginalisation) les résultats de Bob sur le qubit 2.
examples.translation: Ou, en utilisant `marginal_count`, tu peux tracer les résultats de Bob sur le qubit 2.
examples.why: « tracer » in French reads as "to plot/draw"; the quantum-info sense of "trace out" is « tracer partiellement / marginaliser ». Not misleading here because the cell does plot a histogram, but the technical operation named by `marginal_counts` is lost.

examples.source: This subsection will focus on mapping only.
examples.suggested: Cette sous-section se concentrera uniquement sur l'étape de mappage (Mapper le problème).
examples.translation: Cette sous-section se concentrera uniquement sur la cartographie.
examples.why: « cartographie » is the geographic sense; the Qiskit-patterns step is rendered « Mapper le problème » in the very next heading, so the same concept carries two unrelated words within a few lines.

examples.source: Assume they can only communicate with classical communication (like using email or a phone).
examples.suggested: Supposons qu'ils ne puissent communiquer que par communication classique…
examples.translation: Supposons qu'ils ne peuvent communiquer que par communication classique (par e-mail ou par téléphone).
examples.why: « supposons que » governs the subjunctive; « ne peuvent » is a grammatical slip a native technical editor would correct.

examples.source: (Refer to [U-gate] for more information.)
examples.suggested: (Consulte la [porte U] pour plus d'informations.)
examples.translation: (Consulter la [porte U] pour plus d'informations.)
examples.why: The file otherwise holds the informal tu-imperative (« consulte [la référence API] », « Rappelle-toi », « essaie »); this lone infinitive breaks the convention.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — the Holevo caveat ("Le théorème de Holevo est plus général que cela"), the conditional gate rules ($d=1$ → porte $Z$, $c=1$ → porte $X$), the CNOT-then-Hadamard order, the $\mathsf{B}\to c$ / $\mathsf{A}\to d$ measurement assignment, and all four $cd$ cases including the "(Le facteur de phase moins un n'a aucun effet ici.)" caveat are all correct, and core terms (qubit, intrication, e-bit, états de Bell, porte, mesures en base standard) are consistent. What a native technical editor would change is a small set of calques: "Fitting the theme of the lesson" is rendered "Dans le thème de la leçon" (an English-shaped phrase; "En accord avec le thème de la leçon" is the idiom), and "In words, here is what Alice does" becomes the literal "En mots, voici ce qu'Alice fait" ("Autrement dit" / "En clair" is what a French technical writer would use). One small qualifier is dropped: "she sends Bob her qubit" becomes "elle envoie le qubit à Bob", losing the possessive that ties it to $\mathsf{A}$ (recoverable from context, so not misleading). None of these would cause a learner to form a false belief.

examples.source: Fitting the theme of the lesson, one reason why superdense coding is interesting is that it demonstrates a concrete and (in the context of information theory) rather striking use of entanglement.
examples.suggested: En accord avec le thème de la leçon, une raison pour laquelle le codage superdense est intéressant est qu'il illustre une utilisation concrète et (dans le contexte de la théorie de l'information) assez frappante de l'intrication.
examples.translation: Dans le thème de la leçon, une raison pour laquelle le codage superdense est intéressant est qu'il démontre une utilisation concrète et (dans le contexte de la théorie de l'information) assez frappante de l'intrication.
examples.why: "Dans le thème de" is a word-for-word calque of "Fitting the theme of" and is not idiomatic French; a native writer would use "En accord avec le thème de" or "Dans la continuité du thème de". Meaning is preserved, so this is stylistic only.

examples.source: In words, here is what Alice does:
examples.suggested: Autrement dit, voici ce que fait Alice :
examples.translation: En mots, voici ce qu'Alice fait :
examples.why: "En mots" is a literal rendering of "In words" that does not exist as a French discourse marker; "Autrement dit" or "En clair" is the conventional equivalent. Also "ce qu'Alice fait" reads better inverted as "ce que fait Alice".

examples.source: she sends Bob her qubit, and Bob measures to determine which Bell state Alice chose.
examples.suggested: elle envoie son qubit à Bob, et Bob mesure pour déterminer quel état de Bell Alice a choisi.
examples.translation: elle envoie le qubit à Bob, et Bob mesure pour déterminer quel état de Bell Alice a choisi.
examples.why: The possessive "her" is dropped, so "le qubit" no longer explicitly identifies Alice's qubit $\mathsf{A}$ (the one she just acted on) versus the shared pair. Context makes it recoverable, so this is a dropped qualifier rather than a misleading statement.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — the SSVQE weight-priority argument, the VQD penalty/orthogonality chain, and the QSR Fourier-sampling count ($2S+1$ incognite, $T=\prod(2S_i+1)$) all land exactly as in the English, and the informal "tu" register is consistent ("Ti incoraggiamo", "Ricostruirai", "Sentiti libero", "Nei tuoi calcoli"). What a native technical editor would still fix: one outright grammar slip, "si hanno bisogno degli autostati" (line 351; "bisogno" is singular — "servono gli autostati" / "si ha bisogno di"); the calqued adjective order "il più basso autovalore" twice (lines 293, 295) where Italian wants "l'autovalore più basso"; "parametro sintonizzabile" (line 581) for "tunable parameter", where the field says "regolabile"; and "funzionalità interne" (line 534) for "inner workings", which means "features/functionality" rather than "meccanismi interni". Informational, NOT counted as a defect: line 445 renders "transpilation has been built in" as "la traspilazione non è stata integrata" — the inserted negation contradicts the source string but restores the correct meaning (the shown `calculate_overlaps` does not transpile, and the next sentence invites the reader to add it), so the Italian teaches the truth where the EN has a typo.

examples.source: you need the (approximate) eigenstates of the previous $k-1$ eigenvalues
examples.suggested: servono gli autostati (approssimati) dei precedenti $k-1$ autovalori
examples.translation: si hanno bisogno degli autostati (approssimati) dei precedenti $k-1$ autovalori
examples.why: "si hanno bisogno" is ungrammatical — "bisogno" is a singular noun, so the impersonal is "si ha bisogno di"; no native technical writer would produce this agreement.

examples.source: Here, $\lambda_1$ is the lowest eigenvalue from the rest… / to obtain the lowest eigenvalue $\lambda_0$
examples.suggested: l'autovalore più basso tra i rimanenti / per ottenere l'autovalore più basso $\lambda_0$
examples.translation: il più basso autovalore tra gli autovalori rimanenti / per ottenere il più basso autovalore $\lambda_0$
examples.why: Calqued English adjective-before-noun order; Italian technical prose consistently postposes the superlative ("l'autovalore più basso"), and the file itself uses the natural order elsewhere ("lo stato a energia più bassa").

examples.source: adjusting $S_{\max}$ as a tunable parameter (instead of inferring it)
examples.suggested: regolare $S_{\max}$ come parametro regolabile (invece di inferirlo)
examples.translation: regolare $S_{\max}$ come parametro sintonizzabile (invece di inferirlo)
examples.why: "sintonizzabile" is a literal calque of "tunable" that in Italian evokes radio tuning; the conventional term for an adjustable hyper-parameter is "regolabile".

examples.source: while still capturing many of the inner workings and intrinsic properties of quantum computations
examples.suggested: pur catturando molti dei meccanismi interni e delle proprietà intrinseche dei calcoli quantistici
examples.translation: pur catturando molte delle funzionalità interne e delle proprietà intrinseche dei calcoli quantistici
examples.why: "funzionalità" means features/functionality (a software-product sense); "inner workings" here means the internal mechanisms of the computation, i.e. "meccanismi interni".

editor_note: Meaning is fully faithful throughout: the setup scenario (Fatima→`ml`, Ravi→`finance`, Amyra→entrambi i progetti), the "gruppi di accesso senza gruppi di risorse" caveat, the note "Gli utenti non possono essere gestiti finché non accettano l'invito e non effettuano almeno un accesso", and the `quantum-computing.job.delete` rule are all rendered correctly with no drift, hallucination or dropped caveat. Register is consistently informal-tu (Segui, Assicurati, Vai, Consulta, Fai riferimento) and "job"/"chiave API"/"istanze di servizio" are the right, consistent conventions. The only editorial defect is a punctuation artifact repeated three times: the sentence-final period has been pulled INSIDE the link label — "[IAM.](…)", "[Installare Qiskit.](…)", "[documentazione completa di App ID.](…)" — where the English keeps it outside the link. It renders as an underlined period and an editor would move it out; it does not mislead.

examples.source: ...access groups from [IAM](https://cloud.ibm.com/iam/users). / users can review [Install Qiskit](/guides/install-qiskit). / Refer to the full [App ID documentation](...).
examples.suggested: ...da [IAM](https://cloud.ibm.com/iam/users). / consultare [Installare Qiskit](/guides/install-qiskit). / alla [documentazione completa di App ID](...).
examples.translation: ...gruppi di accesso degli utenti da [IAM.](https://cloud.ibm.com/iam/users) / gli utenti possono consultare [Installare Qiskit.](/guides/install-qiskit) / Fai riferimento alla [documentazione completa di App ID.](...)
examples.why: The final period was moved inside the link text in all three cases, so it is rendered as part of the hyperlink label; the English places it outside. Purely cosmetic, no meaning change.

editor_note: No semantic drift and no hallucination: every prose paragraph and all 27 table rows map one-to-one onto the English (regions, routing description, IBM Cloud Logs sentence duplicated exactly as in the source), and informal "tu" holds throughout ("Puoi usare", "Scopri gli eventi"). What a native editor would still change is translationese: the key phrase "eventi di monitoraggio attività" (used 6x, consistently) drops the article in an English-style noun stack — Italian technical prose wants "eventi di monitoraggio delle attività"; likewise "requisiti di audit normativi" reads as calqued word order for "regulatory audit requirements" (better: "requisiti normativi di audit"). "investigare attività anomale" is an anglicism for "indagare su attività anomale". Also, the trailing period was pulled inside the link text ("...Events Routing.](url)"), so the sentence renders with the full stop underlined as part of the link — cosmetic, not misleading.

examples.source: Activity tracking events report on activities that change the state of a service in IBM Cloud.
examples.suggested: Gli eventi di monitoraggio delle attività registrano le operazioni che modificano lo stato di un servizio in IBM Cloud.
examples.translation: Gli eventi di monitoraggio attività registrano le operazioni che modificano lo stato di un servizio in IBM Cloud.
examples.why: "monitoraggio attività" is an English-style noun stack; Italian requires the article ("delle attività"). Consistent across the file, so it is a systematic calque rather than an inconsistency.

examples.source: You can use the events to investigate abnormal activity and critical actions and to comply with regulatory audit requirements.
examples.suggested: Puoi usare gli eventi per indagare su attività anomale e azioni critiche e per soddisfare i requisiti normativi di audit.
examples.translation: Puoi usare gli eventi per investigare attività anomale e azioni critiche, e per soddisfare i requisiti di audit normativi.
examples.why: "investigare" used transitively is an anglicism ("indagare su" is the natural Italian); "requisiti di audit normativi" mirrors English adjective order and leaves "normativi" attached to the wrong noun.

examples.source: For more information, see [About IBM Cloud Activity Tracker Events Routing](https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/atracker?topic=atracker-about).
examples.suggested: Per ulteriori informazioni, consulta [Informazioni su IBM Cloud Activity Tracker Events Routing](https://...).
examples.translation: Per ulteriori informazioni, consulta [Informazioni su IBM Cloud Activity Tracker Events Routing.](https://...)
examples.why: The sentence-final period was moved inside the link label, so it renders as part of the hyperlink. Purely cosmetic, but a native editor would fix it.

editor_note: Substantively faithful throughout — QPU versioning (「リビジョン番号が変更された場合、回路は引き続き実行されます」), the T1/T2 definitions, prob_meas0_prep1/prob_meas1_prep0 conditional probabilities, EPLG/layer-fidelity paragraph and the "error = 1" caveat all match the English, and core terms are correct and consistent (量子ビット, ゲート, トランスパイラー, 基底ゲート, 平均ゲートフィデリティ, カップリングマップ, ランダム化ベンチマーキング). Three things a native technical editor would change. (1) In "Median 2Q error", "batches with a minimum separation of two qubits between edges" was spliced into 「エッジ間の量子ビットの最小分離が2つのバッチです。」 — parsed literally this says the minimum separation *is two batches*, attaching the quantity to the wrong noun; the physics of "measured in isolation" is garbled rather than explained. (2) "Fractional gates" is rendered 分数ゲート, a literal calque; the field keeps フラクショナルゲート. (3) In the error = 1 note, "whether due to poor data quality or other internal factors" is collapsed to 「データの品質が低いなどの内部要因により」, which reclassifies poor data quality as an internal factor and drops the disjunction. Register is clean polite desu/masu with no keigo.

examples.source: Measured in "isolation": batches with a minimum separation of two qubits between edges.
examples.suggested: 「分離」した状態、すなわちエッジ間を最低2量子ビット離したバッチで測定されます。
examples.translation: 「分離」した状態で測定されます。エッジ間の量子ビットの最小分離が2つのバッチです。
examples.why: The splice attaches "two" to バッチ instead of 量子ビット, so the sentence literally asserts that the minimum separation is "two batches". The definition of the isolation condition becomes unparseable for a learner.

examples.source: | Fractional gates | `RX` (single-qubit), `RZZ` (two-qubit) |
examples.suggested: | フラクショナルゲート | `RX`（1量子ビット）, `RZZ`（2量子ビット）|
examples.translation: | 分数ゲート | `RX`（1量子ビット）, `RZZ`（2量子ビット）|
examples.why: 分数ゲート is a literal calque of "fractional"; the Qiskit/IBM Japanese convention keeps フラクショナルゲート for this feature (cf. the use_fractional_gates=True flag referenced later in the same file). Recognizable but not the conventional term.

examples.source: whether due to poor data quality or other internal factors
examples.suggested: データ品質の低下やその他の内部要因により
examples.translation: データの品質が低いなどの内部要因により
examples.why: The English lists two alternatives; the Japanese subsumes poor data quality under 内部要因 as an example of it, dropping the disjunction and slightly narrowing the stated causes.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no drift, no hallucination: the tricky passages all survive intact (ショットは設定間で分割されない/合計 10,240 ショット、`shape` は `samplex_arguments` の暗黙的な形状からブロードキャスト可能でなければならない、表の「1 が 4 に拡張」、単一ランダム化は「ランダム化なしのベース回路と比べて優位性はありません」). Terminology is correct and consistent (古典レジスター、ショット、オブザーバブル、ツワーリング、固有軸/外在軸、samplex kept in English). What a native editor would change is wording only: "ブール値の配列として形式化されます" uses 形式化 (formalization) where "formatted" needs フォーマット/整形; "すべての 5 つの設定を実行し" is an English word-order calque for 5 つの設定すべて; and "各要素はランダムな実現を受け取ります" reads as a literal rendering of "receives a random realization" (実現値 or ランダムな実現が割り当てられます would be idiomatic). Register is correct desu/masu with no keigo.

examples.source: The most common output is bitstring data from measurements, which is formatted as an array of boolean values
examples.suggested: …ブール値の配列としてフォーマットされます。
examples.translation: 最も一般的な出力は測定からのビット文字列データで、ブール値の配列として形式化されます。
examples.why: 形式化 means "formalization" (making something formal/axiomatic), not "formatted". Meaning is still recoverable from context, but no Japanese technical writer would use it for data formatting.

examples.source: The executor runs all five configurations and returns data organized by configuration
examples.suggested: Executor は 5 つの設定すべてを実行し、…
examples.translation: Executor はすべての 5 つの設定を実行し、設定ごとに整理されたデータを返します
examples.why: 「すべての 5 つの…」copies English determiner-before-numeral order; Japanese places すべて after the counted noun phrase. Grammatical but audibly translated.

examples.source: …so even without explicitly requesting multiple randomizations, each element receives a random realization.
examples.suggested: …各要素にはランダムな実現値が割り当てられます。
examples.translation: …明示的に複数のランダム化を要求しなくても、各要素はランダムな実現を受け取ります。
examples.why: "realization" as a bare 実現 reads as the everyday word "realization/achievement" rather than the statistical sense (実現値); 「受け取ります」 for an array element is a calque of "receives".

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — I checked every claim-bearing sentence including the last 40%: the ZNE "not guaranteed to produce an unbiased result" caveat (「偏りのない結果を保証するものではありません」), PEC's "Unlike ZNE, it returns an unbiased estimate … greater overhead", the quadratic-in-γ / exponential-in-depth scaling (「γ の二乗でスケールし、γ 自体はCircuitの深さに対して指数的に」), the coherent-vs-Pauli noise quadratic/linear contrast, and the max_overhead=100 caveat are all correct with no drift, no dropped caveat, and no hallucinated sentence. Two things a native technical editor would still change: (1) a keigo slip in "Next steps" — 「[チュートリアル]をご確認ください」 should be plain 丁寧語 (…を確認してください / チュートリアルもあります) per the informal-register convention; (2) in the ZNE section, "the gate and its inverse" is rendered 「ゲートとその逆行列の等価なシーケンス」 — 逆行列 (inverse matrix) is an odd choice for a gate-level construction where 逆ゲート／逆演算 (U†) is the domain-standard wording. Separately, 「ゲート」 and the kept-English "Gate" alternate within the file (測定Gate / 2量子ビットGate vs CNOTゲート・ゲートトワーリング), which is the deterministic-sweep's scope, not a meaning problem.

examples.source: Check out the [tutorial] on combining error mitigation options with the Estimator primitive.
examples.suggested: Estimatorプリミティブでエラー軽減オプションを組み合わせる[チュートリアル]も確認してください。
examples.translation: Estimatorプリミティブでエラー軽減オプションを組み合わせる[チュートリアル]をご確認ください。
examples.why: 「ご確認ください」 is the honorific register the ja convention excludes; the rest of the page is consistently plain desu/masu, so this one line stands out.

examples.source: two-qubit gates are replaced with equivalent sequences of the gate and its inverse
examples.suggested: 2量子ビットGateを、そのゲートと逆ゲート（逆演算）からなる等価なシーケンスで置き換える
examples.translation: 2量子ビットGateをゲートとその逆行列の等価なシーケンスで置き換える
examples.why: 逆行列 means 'inverse matrix' and reads as a linear-algebra object rather than the circuit-level U† gate being inserted; 逆ゲート／逆演算 is the conventional wording in Japanese Qiskit material. Recognizable, so not misleading, but a native editor would change it.

editor_note: No semantic drift or hallucination: every technical claim tracks the English, including the tricky ones (the Eastin-Knill statement "distância pelo menos 2 … é discreto e, portanto, não é universal", the distiller's "Se qualquer um dos resultados … for 1, o processo falhou" vs "Se … todos … forem 0", and the deliberately counterintuitive source claim that a logical X is realized by Z⊗I⊗I…, which the translation faithfully preserves rather than "fixing"). Terminology is correct and consistent throughout (bloco de código, gadget transversal, produto tensorial, estado gato, medições de síndrome, destilação de estados mágicos, código de superfície/de cores). What a native technical editor would still fix are grammar and calque slips: "um erro de alto peso que o código não consegue lidar" is missing the obligatory preposition ("com o qual o código não consegue lidar"); "poderia-se potencialmente usar" is an ill-formed clitic placement (should be "seria possível usar" or "poder-se-ia"); and several phrases are word-order calques of the English ("o qubit segundo a partir do topo", "Adicionando à nossa preocupação está o fato de que", "ilustra como este processo parece no nível mais alto"). None of these mislead the learner.

examples.source: it could turn a low-weight error into a high-weight error that the code cannot handle.
examples.suggested: …em um erro de alto peso com o qual o código não consegue lidar.
examples.translation: poderia transformar um erro de baixo peso em um erro de alto peso que o código não consegue lidar.
examples.why: "lidar" requires the preposition "com"; the relative clause as written is ungrammatical in Portuguese and reads as raw MT.

examples.source: one could potentially use a surface or color code for error correction
examples.suggested: seria possível usar um código de superfície ou de cores para correção de erros
examples.translation: poderia-se potencialmente usar um código de superfície ou de cores para correção de erros
examples.why: "poderia-se" is an invalid clitic placement (would need mesoclisis "poder-se-ia"); a native technical writer would rephrase with "seria possível" or "pode-se".

examples.source: both the control and target for the second CNOT is the qubit second from top
examples.suggested: …é o segundo qubit a partir do topo
examples.translation: tanto o controle quanto o alvo do segundo CNOT é o qubit segundo a partir do topo
examples.why: "o qubit segundo a partir do topo" copies English adjective placement; Portuguese puts the ordinal before the noun.

examples.source: Adding to our concern is the fact that subsequent two-qubit gates might propagate these errors even further
examples.suggested: Outro motivo de preocupação é que gates de dois qubits subsequentes podem propagar esses erros ainda mais
examples.translation: Adicionando à nossa preocupação está o fato de que gates de dois qubits subsequentes podem propagar esses erros ainda mais
examples.why: Direct calque of the English cleft construction; the gerund-initial clause is not idiomatic in Portuguese expository prose.

examples.source: This could actually be challenging for some codes selected to make it so, but for a CSS code it's a matter of measuring each physical qubit followed by classical post-processing.
examples.suggested: Isso pode, de fato, ser difícil para alguns códigos, mas para um código CSS basta medir cada qubit físico e fazer um pós-processamento clássico.
examples.translation: Isso poderia ser de fato desafiador para alguns códigos selecionados para torná-lo assim, mas para um código CSS é uma questão de medir cada qubit físico seguido de pós-processamento clássico.
examples.why: The source clause is already awkward; the word-for-word rendering "códigos selecionados para torná-lo assim" is opaque in Portuguese and the parenthetical loses its explanatory force for the learner.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no drift, no hallucination, no dropped caveat: the noise-model setup, the "compute-uncompute" rationale ($|000000\rangle$, $\langle IIIIIZ\rangle = 1$), the "$4k$ camadas de portas de dois qubits" note, and the resilience-level explanation all match the English exactly, and core terms (observável, valores esperados, modelo de ruído, sampler/Estimator/backend/shots kept in English) are correct and consistent. Two things a native technical editor would still change: (1) "circuitos de computo-descomputo" is an ad-hoc coinage and, unaccented, reads as the verb forms "computo/descomputo" rather than nouns — PT practice is to keep "compute-uncompute" (optionally glossed), e.g. "circuitos compute-uncompute (computa–descomputa)"; (2) the same heading "Plot results" is rendered two ways in the same file — "2.5 Visualizar resultados" vs "3.4 Plotar os resultados". Neither misleads a learner.

examples.source: we use compute-uncompute circuits that consist of a first stage where the original circuit $U$ is applied
examples.suggested: usamos circuitos compute-uncompute (computa–descomputa), que consistem em uma primeira etapa em que o circuito original $U$ é aplicado
examples.translation: usamos circuitos de computo-descomputo, que consistem em uma primeira etapa onde o circuito original $U$ é aplicado
examples.why: "computo-descomputo" is an invented compound and, without the accent, parses as the 1st-person verb forms rather than nouns; the field normally keeps "compute-uncompute" in English, optionally glossed. Meaning survives, so this is cosmetic, not misleading.

examples.source: ### 2.5 Plot results  …  ### 3.4 Plot results
examples.suggested: Use one rendering for both, e.g. "Plotar os resultados" in 2.5 and 3.4
examples.translation: ### 2.5 Visualizar resultados  …  ### 3.4 Plotar os resultados
examples.why: The identical English heading is rendered two different ways within the same file; harmless for comprehension but an inconsistency a native editor would unify.

editor_note: Fiel e natural em todo o texto, sem deriva semântica: as três motivações em bullets preservam exatamente as condições do inglês ("classe mais ampla de estados", "partes isoladas de sistemas ... emaranhado com outro sistema que desejamos ignorar", "estados clássicos (probabilísticos) ... diagonais"), a ressalva "embora matrizes de densidade sejam de fato matrizes, elas representam estados — não ações ou operações" está intacta, e a terminologia central está correta e consistente (density matrices→matrizes de densidade, eigenvalues→autovalores, linear mappings→mapeamentos lineares, entangled→emaranhado, stochastic matrices→matrizes estocásticas), com "você" informal no parágrafo do vídeo; a única observação fora do escopo de prosa é que a string do prop DefinitionTooltip e o title do IBMVideo permanecem em inglês.

Meaning is faithful throughout — the load-bearing physics survives intact: the superposition caveat ("Ang superposition ay hindi nangangahulugan na makikita mo ang parehong resulta sa isang sukat"), the QPU-vs-simulator contrast ("may ilang occurrences ng $01$ o $10$ dahil sa noise" vs "na walang occurrences ng $01$ o $10$"), the CX control/target assignment, and the coin-flip statistical-fluctuation analogy are all correct, and domain terms (qubit, gate, superposition, entanglement, shots, backend, transpiling, Sampler) are kept in English consistently. What a native technical editor would change is a scattering of English-shaped calques and small agreement slips: "Lakaran ito sa sarili mong takbo" for "Work through it at your own pace", "Ang mga trabaho ay maaaring umupo sa queue" (literal "sit"), "Higit pa rito mamaya" for "More on this later", and "mauuna ka na sa laro" for "ahead of the game". Two spots are grammatically off rather than merely stiff: "ang mga sukat ay maaaring maling minsan" (should be "mali minsan") and "para gumamit ang lahat ng parehong tools" (should be "para magamit ng lahat ang parehong tools"). Also "Ito ay biswal sa tinatawag na circuit diagram" drops the verb of "It's visualized in…" — recoverable, but incomplete as written. None of these mislead; register stays casual with no po/opo.

examples.source: Work through it at your own pace.
examples.suggested: Gawin mo ito sa sarili mong bilis.
examples.translation: Lakaran ito sa sarili mong takbo.
examples.why: Literal calque: 'lakaran' means physically walk over something and 'takbo' means running speed; a Tagalog technical writer would say 'sa sarili mong bilis'.

examples.source: Jobs can sit in a queue, because many people may be using the same device.
examples.suggested: Maaaring maghintay muna ang mga job sa queue, dahil maraming tao ang posibleng gumagamit ng parehong device.
examples.translation: Ang mga trabaho ay maaaring umupo sa queue, dahil maraming tao ang maaaring gumagamit ng parehong device.
examples.why: 'umupo' is the physical act of sitting down; English idiomatic 'sit in a queue' calqued literally. 'Maghintay sa queue' is the natural rendering.

examples.source: It's visualized in what is called a circuit diagram, where the qubits are represented by horizontal lines...
examples.suggested: Ipinapakita ito nang biswal sa tinatawag na circuit diagram, kung saan...
examples.translation: Ito ay biswal sa tinatawag na circuit diagram, kung saan ang mga qubit ay kinakatawan ng mga horizontal line...
examples.why: 'Ito ay biswal' reads as 'it is visual' — the verb of 'is visualized' is dropped, leaving an adjective where a predicate is needed.

examples.source: ...measurements can be wrong sometimes, and device calibration drifts over time.
examples.suggested: ...maaaring mali kung minsan ang mga sukat, at nagbabago ang device calibration sa paglipas ng panahon.
examples.translation: ...ang mga sukat ay maaaring maling minsan, at ang device calibration ay nagbabago sa paglipas ng panahon.
examples.why: 'maaaring maling minsan' is an agreement/linker slip — the linker -ng on 'mali' has nothing to attach to; should be 'mali kung minsan' or 'mali minsan'.

examples.source: In Colab, we install dependencies inside the notebook so everyone runs the same tools.
examples.suggested: ...para magamit ng lahat ang parehong tools.
examples.translation: Sa Colab, ini-install natin ang mga dependency sa loob ng notebook para gumamit ang lahat ng parehong tools.
examples.why: Focus/case mismatch: 'para gumamit ang lahat ng parehong tools' puts 'lahat' in the wrong role and reads ungrammatically; the intended sense is 'so that everyone uses the same tools'.

examples.source: More on this later.
examples.suggested: Babalikan natin ito mamaya.
examples.translation: Higit pa rito mamaya.
examples.why: Word-for-word calque of the English fragment; 'Higit pa rito' means 'more than this' and does not carry the 'we'll cover this later' sense.

editor_note: No misleading content: all the math prose (probability-vector properties, the M|a⟩=|f(a)⟩ requirement, stochastic-column sums, the non-commutativity example, the "measurement changes knowledge, not the system" caveat with the second observer) is faithfully carried over, and ket/bra/bracket, "standard basis vector", "probability vector", "stochastic na matris" are consistent. What a native technical editor would still change: "For the sake of tidiness" is rendered "Para sa kadakilaan" ("for greatness"), a plainly wrong word; "arbitrary choice" is rendered "di-makatwirang pagpili" ("unreasonable choice") twice (the intended mathematical sense is "kahit anong / arbitraryong pagpili" — universality survives only because "palaging posible" and "anumang stochastic na matris" remain); and "corresponding to" is rendered throughout as "katumbas ng" ("equal to") rather than "tumutugma sa". Naturalness slips: sentence-initial "Pala," (the enclitic cannot open a sentence), the calques "Intuwitibong nagsasalita" and "ang paraan ng pagtatrabaho ng quantum na impormasyon" ("pagtatrabaho" = laboring, should be "paggana"), plus the misspellings "konfigurasyon" and "beripikasiyon". Two small drifts: "This may seem trivial" → "Maaaring mukhang walang kahulugan ito" ("seems meaningless"), and "in a later lesson" → "sa susunod na aralin" ("in the next lesson"). Informal register holds throughout (no po/opo).

examples.source: For the sake of tidiness, we write this product as ⟨a|b⟩ rather than ⟨a||b⟩.
examples.suggested: Para sa kaayusan/kalinisan ng sulat, isinusulat natin ang produktong ito bilang ⟨a|b⟩ ...
examples.translation: Para sa kadakilaan, isinusulat natin ang produktong ito bilang ⟨a|b⟩ sa halip na ⟨a||b⟩.
examples.why: "kadakilaan" means greatness/majesty, not tidiness — a plainly wrong word choice that makes the clause nonsensical, though it does not affect the math.

examples.source: For an arbitrary choice of a classical state set, we can describe the set of all probabilistic operations ... / Such an expression is always possible, for an arbitrary choice of a classical state set
examples.suggested: Para sa kahit anong (arbitraryong) pagpili ng set ng klasikal na estado, ...
examples.translation: Para sa isang di-makatwirang pagpili ng isang set ng klasikal na estado, ...
examples.why: "di-makatwiran" = unreasonable/capricious; the mathematical sense is "any whatsoever". The generality claim is only rescued by the surviving "palaging posible" and "anumang stochastic na matris".

examples.source: As it turns out, the Dirac notation is not specific to quantum information
examples.suggested: Lumalabas na hindi eksklusibo sa quantum na impormasyon ang notasyong Dirac
examples.translation: Pala, ang notasyong Dirac ay hindi eksklusibo sa quantum na impormasyon
examples.why: "pala" is an enclitic particle and cannot open a sentence in Tagalog; a native writer would use "Lumalabas na ..." or "Sa katunayan, ...".

examples.source: the way quantum information works might seem less unusual
examples.suggested: ang paraan ng paggana ng quantum na impormasyon ay maaaring mukhang hindi gaanong kakaiba
examples.translation: ang paraan ng pagtatrabaho ng quantum na impormasyon ay maaaring mukhang hindi gaanong kakaiba
examples.why: "pagtatrabaho" means laboring/holding a job; "works" in the sense of "functions" is "paggana". Same paragraph also has the calque "Intuwitibong nagsasalita" for "Intuitively speaking".

examples.source: This may seem trivial, and in some sense it is.
examples.suggested: Maaaring mukhang napakasimple/walang kabuluhan ito, at sa ilang paraan nga ay ganoon.
examples.translation: Maaaring mukhang walang kahulugan ito, at sa ilang paraan ay ganoon nga.
examples.why: "walang kahulugan" = meaningless; the English says the observation is obvious/trivial, not devoid of meaning — the teaching beat (obvious classically, strange quantumly) is blunted.

examples.source: As we will discuss in greater detail later in a later lesson, ⟨a|b⟩ may also be seen as an inner product
examples.suggested: Tulad ng tatalakayin nang mas detalyado sa isang susunod na aralin, ...
examples.translation: Tulad ng tatalakayin nang mas detalyado sa susunod na aralin, ang ⟨a|b⟩ ay maaari ring makita bilang isang inner product
examples.why: "sa susunod na aralin" promises the immediately next lesson; the English only says "a later lesson".

examples.source: the matrices M1,…,M4 corresponding to the functions f1,…,f4 / a 1 in the entry corresponding to the pair (b,a)
examples.suggested: ... na tumutugma sa mga function ... / sa entry na tumutugma sa pares na (b,a)
examples.translation: ang mga matris na M1,…,M4 na katumbas ng mga function ... / isang 1 sa entry na katumbas ng pares na (b,a)
examples.why: "katumbas" means "equal/equivalent to"; "corresponding to" is "tumutugma sa". Used consistently, so recognizable, but it says the matrix equals the function rather than represents it.

editor_note: One sentence inverts a load-bearing instruction: EN "specifically by taking Z⊗I⊗Z in place of either of the generators we did select" becomes "lalo na sa PAG-ALIS ng Z⊗I⊗Z bilang kapalit ng alinman sa mga generator na pinili natin" — "pag-alis" means *removal*, the opposite of taking/using, so the learner is told to remove an operator that is not currently a generator, breaking the point that a different generating set yields the same stabilizer ("pagkuha"/"paggamit" is what's meant). Secondary meaning slips: line 143 uses "katuwiran" (= *reason/justification*) where EN has the appositive "namely", and line 153 renders "which we'll define precisely in the next section" as "na tiyak na ibibigay natin" (= *which we will certainly give*), dropping "define". Naturalness slips elsewhere are minor but real: "sa gitna ng 64 posibleng ... Pauli operation" is a literal calque of "among the 64", "aside" becomes "karagdagang paalala" (*additional reminder*), and "susukathin" (line 36) is a typo for "susukatin". Core terminology (stabilizer generator, syndrome, eigenvector/eigenvalue, "hindi-mapanirang pagsukat" for nondestructive measurement, commute/anti-commute kept in English) is correct and consistent, and the informal register holds throughout.

examples.source: specifically by taking $Z\otimes\mathbb{I}\otimes Z$ in place of either of the generators we did select
examples.suggested: lalo na sa pagkuha ng $Z\otimes\mathbb{I}\otimes Z$ bilang kapalit ng alinman sa mga generator na pinili natin
examples.translation: lalo na sa pag-alis ng $Z\otimes\mathbb{I}\otimes Z$ bilang kapalit ng alinman sa mga generator na pinili natin
examples.why: 'pag-alis' means removal — the reverse of 'taking'. The sentence now instructs removing Z⊗I⊗Z, which is not one of the two chosen generators, so the substitution that keeps the stabilizer unchanged no longer makes sense.

examples.source: into two subspaces of equal dimension, namely the space of $+1$ eigenvectors and the space of $-1$ eigenvectors
examples.suggested: ...na may pantay na dimensyon, samakatuwid ang espasyo ng mga $+1$ eigenvector at ang espasyo ng mga $-1$ eigenvector
examples.translation: sa dalawang subspace na may pantay na dimensyon, katuwiran ang espasyo ng mga $+1$ eigenvector at ang espasyo ng mga $-1$ eigenvector
examples.why: 'katuwiran' means reason/justification and is not an appositive marker; it reads as a mangled word where 'namely' (samakatuwid / ibig sabihin) belongs.

examples.source: are true in general for stabilizer codes, which we'll define precisely in the next section
examples.suggested: ...para sa mga stabilizer code, na tiyak na tutukuyin natin sa susunod na seksyon
examples.translation: ay totoo sa pangkalahatan para sa mga stabilizer code, na tiyak na ibibigay natin sa susunod na seksyon
examples.why: 'define precisely' becomes 'will certainly give'; the adverb 'precisely' is re-read as 'certainly' and the verb 'define' is lost, weakening the forward reference to the formal definition.

examples.source: and among the 64 possible 3-qubit Pauli operations, there are exactly 16 of them in this category
examples.suggested: at sa 64 na posibleng 3-qubit Pauli operation, eksaktong 16 ang nasa kategoryang ito
examples.translation: at sa gitna ng 64 posibleng 3-qubit Pauli operation, mayroon nang eksakto 16 sa kategoryang ito
examples.why: 'sa gitna ng' is a spatial calque of 'among' that a native technical writer would not use for set membership; 'mayroon nang eksakto 16' is also ungrammatical ('mayroong').

examples.source: and measure both using the circuits suggested at the end of the previous section
examples.suggested: at susukatin ang pareho gamit ang mga circuit na iminungkahi sa dulo ng nakaraang seksyon
examples.translation: at susukathin ang pareho gamit ang mga circuit na iminungkahi sa dulo ng nakaraang seksyon
examples.why: 'susukathin' is a typo for 'susukatin'; it is not a Tagalog word form.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no drift, no hallucination: the region caveat ("Ти можеш отримати доступ до будь-якого регіону за допомогою одного ключа API, але бачитимеш і матимеш доступ лише до екземплярів, створених у тому регіоні, в який ти увійшов") preserves both halves of the English condition, and the "profile ≠ IBM Cloud account" warning in step 2 is intact. Two surface defects a native editor would fix: (1) the very first sentence has a malformed imperative "— зверниться до свого адміністратора" — the informal form is "звернися" ("зверніться" would be the formal one), so as written it is neither, and it also breaks the file's otherwise consistent "ти" register; (2) the Next-steps link is rendered "Запусти свою першу схему на реальному залізі", where "залізо" is slangy shop-talk for hardware — documentation register calls for "на реальному обладнанні" / "на квантовому обладнанні". Neither misleads; core terms (екземпляр, токен API, робочі навантаження, квантові процесори (QPU)) are correct and consistent.

examples.source: If you do not have an invitation from an administrator to join an account that an administrator set up, contact your administrator.
examples.suggested: … — звернися до свого адміністратора.
examples.translation: Якщо ти не отримав запрошення від адміністратора для приєднання до облікового запису, який він налаштував, — зверниться до свого адміністратора.
examples.why: "зверниться" is not a valid imperative: informal is "звернися", formal is "зверніться". It also clashes with the file's informal "ти" convention used everywhere else (Прийми, Увійди, Перейди, Переконайся).

examples.source: Follow the steps in the [Run your first circuit on hardware] guide to write and run a quantum program.
examples.suggested: Запусти свою першу схему на реальному обладнанні
examples.translation: Виконай кроки з розділу [Запусти свою першу схему на реальному залізі], щоб написати та запустити квантову програму.
examples.why: "залізо" is colloquial slang for hardware; in technical documentation the conventional rendering is "обладнання" (or "квантове обладнання"). Informal address does not extend to slang lexis.

editor_note: No semantic drift anywhere: every build step, path variable, caveat (Python needed only for dynamic linking, never initialized at runtime; the warnings from `make c` are expected; rpath alternative) is carried across faithfully, and the informal "ти" convention holds consistently ("дивись", "прочитай", "зверни увагу", "виконай", "скомпілюй"). Two things a native technical editor would still change: in the Windows requirements, "native command prompt" is rendered as "рідний командний рядок", where "рідний" is a literal calque of the wrong sense of "native" (it reads as "dear/one's own"); a Ukrainian technical writer would write "нативний командний рядок" or, better, "власний командний рядок MSVC". Also "Якщо бібліотека Python не доступна за замовчуванням" should be the single word "недоступна" per Ukrainian orthography. Neither misleads; terminology is otherwise correct and consistent (observable → "спостережувана величина (observable)", header → "заголовковий файл", linking → "компонування", shared library → "спільна бібліотека" used consistently).

examples.source: A C compiler: for example, MSVC and the native command prompt offering the ``cl`` command
examples.suggested: Компілятор C: наприклад, MSVC і його власний (нативний) командний рядок із командою ``cl``
examples.translation: Компілятор C: наприклад, MSVC і рідний командний рядок із командою ``cl``
examples.why: "рідний" is a calque picking the wrong sense of "native"; in Ukrainian IT prose it reads as "dear/own kin", not "platform-native". Meaning is still recoverable, so MINOR.

examples.source: If the Python library is not available per default during dynamic linking, this also needs to be added.
examples.suggested: Якщо бібліотека Python недоступна за замовчуванням під час динамічного компонування, її також потрібно додати.
examples.translation: Якщо бібліотека Python не доступна за замовчуванням під час динамічного компонування, її також потрібно додати.
examples.why: Ukrainian orthography requires the single word "недоступна" here (no contrast is being drawn); the split spelling is a typo-level slip, not a meaning change.

examples.source: This code verifies that everything has been installed:
examples.suggested: Ці команди перевіряють, що все встановлено:
examples.translation: Ці команди перевіряють, що все встановлено правильно:
examples.why: Adds "правильно" (correctly), a qualifier not in the source — the version checks only confirm presence, not correctness. Too small to mislead, noted for completeness.

editor_note: Meaning is substantively faithful throughout — the tricky "unless" construction in the billing answer is correctly rendered as a double negative ("Кошти не буде списано, якщо ти не створиш ... і не будеш надсилати"), the three-year retention figure, the "only us-east supports the Open Plan" caveat, and the "bearer token cannot authenticate to Qiskit Runtime" restriction all survive intact, and informal "ти" holds everywhere. The main defect is lexical: "credential" is rendered twice as «обліковий запис» (= *user account*), so the bearer-token section literally asserts "Токен API — це довгостроковий обліковий запис" / "Токен Bearer — це тимчасовий обліковий запис"; the correct term is «облікові дані» (or simply «тимчасові/довгострокові облікові дані»). The long-lived-vs-temporary distinction still comes across, so this does not derail the lesson, but it is a wrong term a native editor would fix. Two sentences are also ungrammatical rather than merely stiff: "Квантові процесорні блоки у статті слід посилатися..." (nominative subject with impersonal «слід посилатися» — needs "На квантові процесорні блоки ... слід посилатися") and the heading "Я не бачу щось в інтерфейсі користувача, наприклад завдань адміністрування" (case mismatch: «чогось ... наприклад, завдань» or «щось ... наприклад, завдання»).

examples.source: An API token is a long-lived credential used to authenticate to the Qiskit Runtime service. A bearer token is a temporary credential ...
examples.suggested: Токен API — це довгострокові облікові дані, які використовуються для автентифікації в сервісі Qiskit Runtime. Токен Bearer — це тимчасові облікові дані ...
examples.translation: Токен API — це довгостроковий обліковий запис, що використовується для автентифікації в сервісі Qiskit Runtime. Токен Bearer — це тимчасовий обліковий запис ...
examples.why: «обліковий запис» is the established Ukrainian term for *user account*, not *credential*; as written the text states that a token IS an account. The long-lived/temporary contrast still reads correctly, so it is a wrong-word slip rather than a misleading claim, but it must be «облікові дані».

examples.source: Quantum processing units in the paper should be referenced by their unique name (for example, `ibmq_vigo`)
examples.suggested: На квантові процесорні блоки у статті слід посилатися за їхньою унікальною назвою (наприклад, `ibmq_vigo`)
examples.translation: Квантові процесорні блоки у статті слід посилатися за їхньою унікальною назвою (наприклад, `ibmq_vigo`)
examples.why: Calqued English word order leaves a nominative subject attached to the impersonal predicate «слід посилатися»; no native technical writer would produce this — the preposition «на» + accusative is required.

examples.source: I don't see something in the user interface, such as my administration tasks.
examples.suggested: Я не бачу чогось в інтерфейсі користувача, наприклад завдань адміністрування.
examples.translation: Я не бачу щось в інтерфейсі користувача, наприклад завдань адміністрування.
examples.why: Case mismatch inside the sentence: «щось» (accusative) is followed by the genitive «завдань», and negated «не бачу» normally takes the genitive «чогось». Also missing the comma after «наприклад».

examples.source: Cite Qiskit by using the included BibTeX file.
examples.suggested: Цитуй Qiskit, використовуючи доданий файл BibTeX.
examples.translation: Цитуй Qiskit, використовуючи вкладений файл BibTeX.
examples.why: «вкладений» reads as *nested/enclosed (in an envelope)*; for a file shipped with the repository the idiomatic choice is «доданий» or «наведений». Meaning is recoverable, so this is purely a word-choice slip.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no inversion, no dropped caveat, no hallucinated claim — and the informal singular address (يمكنك استخدام…) is consistent, so nothing here would mislead a learner. Three wording slips a native technical editor would still change: "visualize … events" is rendered "لتصوير الأحداث" (reads as "photograph/depict the events"; the conventional rendering is تمثيل/عرض الأحداث بصريًا) in both line 16 and line 27; "an IBM Cloud Logs instance" becomes "نسخة IBM Cloud Logs" (نسخة = copy) where the standard IT term is مثيل, and the English indefinite is flattened; and the appositive construction "…وإنشاء تنبيهات بشأنها، تلك الأحداث التي تُولَّد في حسابك" is a stiff calque of the English relative clause that an Arabic writer would restructure (…الأحداث التي تُولَّد في حسابك ويُوجّهها … لتمثيلها وإنشاء تنبيهات بشأنها). Separately, the Arabic Action/Triggered-by table carries two rows the English source does not have (`Get job transpiled circuits` and `List job interim results` under `quantum-computing.job.read`) — valid endpoints, so not misleading, but a source-divergence worth reconciling.

examples.source: You can use IBM Cloud Logs to visualize and alert on events that are generated in your account
examples.suggested: يمكنك استخدام IBM Cloud Logs لعرض الأحداث بصريًا وإنشاء تنبيهات بشأنها
examples.translation: يمكنك استخدام IBM Cloud Logs لتصوير الأحداث وإنشاء تنبيهات بشأنها
examples.why: «تصوير» means photographing/depicting; for UI "visualize" Arabic technical docs use التمثيل/العرض البصري. Recognizable but not the conventional term, and it repeats in both occurrences.

examples.source: routed … to an IBM Cloud Logs instance
examples.suggested: ويُوجّهها … إلى مثيل (instance) من IBM Cloud Logs
examples.translation: ويُوجّهها … إلى نسخة IBM Cloud Logs
examples.why: «نسخة» means copy; the established rendering for a cloud service instance is مثيل. The indefinite "an … instance" is also flattened to a definite-sounding phrase.

examples.source: to visualize and alert on events that are generated in your account and routed by … to an IBM Cloud Logs instance
examples.suggested: لعرض الأحداث التي تُولَّد في حسابك ويُوجّهها IBM Cloud Activity Tracker Event Routing إلى مثيل IBM Cloud Logs، وإنشاء تنبيهات بشأنها
examples.translation: لتصوير الأحداث وإنشاء تنبيهات بشأنها، تلك الأحداث التي تُولَّد في حسابك ويُوجّهها IBM Cloud Activity Tracker Event Routing إلى نسخة IBM Cloud Logs
examples.why: The resumptive appositive «، تلك الأحداث التي» is a calque used to rescue the English trailing relative clause; an Arabic technical writer would place the relative clause on the noun directly.

examples.source: (rows absent from the English table)
examples.suggested: drop the two extra rows, or propagate them to the EN source
examples.translation: | `quantum-computing.job.read` | Get job transpiled circuits (`GET /v1/jobs/{id}/transpiled_circuits`) | and | `quantum-computing.job.read` | List job interim results (`GET /v1/jobs/{id}/interim_results`) |
examples.why: The Arabic action table has 29 rows against the English 27. The endpoints are real so no learner is misled, but the translated page asserts coverage the source does not — a content divergence to reconcile.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no inverted conditions, no swapped quantities (50 كيوبت, 100 كيوبت, 15 مايو 2024 all correct), the Open-Plan caveat and the "local testing mode has no built-in error suppression/mitigation, you must specify it explicitly" note are both intact, and the informal register (يمكنك, مهاراتك) holds. Three wordings a native technical editor would still change: "Hands-on experience with quantum hardware" is rendered "العمل الميداني مع الأجهزة الكمية", which means field work and is the wrong register for lab/hands-on practice; "configuration" in the ansatz bullet becomes the awkward coinage "الضبط الإعدادي" inside an already repetitive "تضبيط… يعني ضبط…" sentence; and "exponential growth" is rendered "التضاعف الأسي" (exponential doubling) where "النمو الأسي" is the standard term. Also minor: "performing noisy simulations of the QPU" loses "of the QPU" (just "إجراء محاكاة مع ضوضاء"), and transpiler is consistently but weakly rendered "المُحوِّل" — recognizable, not misleading.

examples.source: Hands-on experience with quantum hardware develops a deeper understanding of quantum phenomena
examples.suggested: تُعمّق الخبرة العملية المباشرة مع الأجهزة الكمية فهم الظواهر الكمية
examples.translation: يُعمّق العمل الميداني مع الأجهزة الكمية فهم الظواهر الكمية
examples.why: "العمل الميداني" means field work (surveys, on-site data collection); it is the wrong register for hands-on lab/hardware practice. Nuance shifts but the learner is not misled.

examples.source: Fine-tuning algorithms for quantum hardware involves adjusting ansatz, circuit implementations, parameters, and configuration to maximize performance.
examples.suggested: يشمل الضبط الدقيق للخوارزميات على الأجهزة الكمية تعديل الـ ansatz وتنفيذات الدوائر والمعاملات والإعدادات لتحقيق أقصى أداء.
examples.translation: تضبيط الخوارزميات للعمل على الأجهزة الكمية يعني ضبط الـ ansatz وتنفيذات الدوائر والمعاملات والضبط الإعدادي لتحقيق أقصى أداء.
examples.why: "الضبط الإعدادي" is a non-idiomatic coinage for "configuration" (standard: الإعدادات), and it lands inside a تضبيط…ضبط…الضبط repetition no native technical writer would leave.

examples.source: This ceiling comes from the exponential growth in computational resources required
examples.suggested: ينبع هذا السقف من النمو الأسي في الموارد الحسابية اللازمة
examples.translation: ينبثق هذا السقف من التضاعف الأسي في الموارد الحسابية اللازمة
examples.why: "التضاعف الأسي" says exponential doubling rather than exponential growth; the standard Arabic term is النمو الأسي. Recognizable, so MINOR only.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — I checked every claim-bearing paragraph including the broadcasting rules, the four examples, and the BitArray/post-processing section at the end, and found no inverted conditions, swapped shapes, or dropped caveats (the commuting-observables Admonition, the "at most four/three values" counts, the 5×1/1×1, 5×1/5×1, 1×6/4×1, 3×6/3×1 example shapes, and the left-most/right-most axis description all match). What a native technical editor would change is terminology consistency and a few agreement slips: "primitive" is kept in English almost everywhere ("Estimator primitive"، "الـ primitives") but is suddenly translated as "البدائيات" in the heading "نظرة عامة على مخرجات البدائيات" and as "بدائية Estimator" in the Estimator-output section; "method" is rendered "أسلوب `run()`" early on but "تابع `get_count`" / "التوابع" later in the same file. "commuting observables" is rendered "observable-ان متبادلان" — recognizable but imprecise (commuting is تبادلي/قابل للتبديل, whereas متبادل reads as "mutual"). There are also two gender-agreement slips ("فلن يُقدَّر قيمهما" should be تُقدَّر; "يصبح كل قيمة معاملة عمودًا" should be تصبح). None of these would mislead a learner.

examples.source: ## Overview of primitive outputs / the data returned in the `PubResult` for the Estimator primitive

editor_note: The translation is fluent and technically accurate almost everywhere (venv workflow, single-`pip install` rule, `qiskit-terra` conflict, `pipdeptree` diagnosis, tox/Actions guidance all track the English), but the closing Admonition of the "Qiskit v1.0 の動作する環境を作成する" section inverts a negation: EN "it was not known to support Qiskit v1.0 yet, so it marked that in its requirements" becomes 「Qiskit v1.0 をサポートしていないことが判明していなかったため、要件にそのことが記載されていたのです」 — i.e. "because it had NOT been established that it does NOT support v1.0, it recorded that". The result is a self-contradictory causal claim: the reader is told the pin was added because the lack of support was unknown, which is the opposite of the English (support was unconfirmed, so the package declared `qiskit<1`). Secondary, non-blocking: two keigo slips against the informal convention (「ご確認ください」, 「お問い合わせください」) and a dropped qualifier where "a bash-like syntax" becomes plain 「bash 構文」.

examples.why: Negation inversion: the English says support was not yet KNOWN (unconfirmed), which is why the package declared `qiskit<1`. The Japanese says it had not been established that it does NOT support v1.0 — the opposite epistemic state — making the stated reason for the pin a non-sequitur and teaching the reader a false account of why the example distribution behaved as it did.

editor_note: The prose is fluent, natural Japanese in consistent desu/masu with no keigo, and every substantive instruction (API key creation, CRN copying, `set_as_default`/`overwrite` semantics, the "`instance` が指定されている場合は無視されます" caveat repeated for plans_preference/region/tags, and both worked examples) matches the English faithfully — no inverted conditions, swapped quantities or dropped caveats. Three editorial slips remain: (1) step 3 of 始める前に adds "IBMidまたはGoogleアカウントで" which has no counterpart in the English ("Log in to IBM Quantum Platform."), an unsourced addition that implies those are the accepted login methods; (2) the Next-steps bullet renames the linked guide from "Run your first circuit on hardware" to "[Hello world]", losing the descriptive title the English uses to tell the reader what the guide does; (3) the `instance` option line stacks 使用 three times ("IBM Cloud CRNまたはインスタンス名を使用して、使用するインスタンスをオプションで指定します"), which a native technical writer would rewrite. None of these teaches a false concept, so this is MINOR rather than FAIL.

examples.source: Follow the steps in the [Run your first circuit on hardware](/guides/hello-world) guide to write and run a quantum program.
