editor_note: No semantic drift: every quantity, condition and caveat survives intact — the negation in "Não serás cobrado a menos que cries uma instância Pay-As-You-Go Plan e a uses para enviar cargas de trabalho para QPUs", the date "antes de 25 de outubro de 2021", and the cost warning "Todos os jobs enviados para QPUs ao especificar esta instância terão um custo associado" all match the English. Two editorial slips only. (1) The contrastive "instead" in "follow the steps in [Install Qiskit] instead" is dropped — "segue os passos em [Instalar o Qiskit]." loses the "em vez disso / em alternativa" that signals this guide does not apply to that reader. (2) The page's key term is rendered as "fazer upgrade" everywhere (title, headings, steps) except step 4, where "your account is upgraded" becomes "a tua conta é atualizada" — "atualizada" reads as "updated" and breaks the term's consistency at exactly the point of payoff. Register is coherent European-Portuguese informal tu ("segue", "cria", "se tiveres", "utilizadores"); the Brazilian-style link label "Execute seu primeiro circuito em hardware" is not a defect since it reproduces the pt hello-world page title verbatim.

examples.source: If you are an individual setting up the service for the first time or if you have been invited to an instance by an administrator, follow the steps in [Install Qiskit](/guides/install-qiskit) instead.

examples.source: After your payment information is processed, your account is upgraded.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no drift, no hallucination, no dropped caveat; the tricky passages (o Target "pode conter instruções que operam em mais de dois qubit (que não podem ser representadas em um CouplingMap)", "que pode ser apenas um subconjunto da informação contida no objeto Target", version vs. backend_version distinction) all track the English exactly, and the informal "você" convention holds ("os pequenos ajustes que você precisa fazer"). What a native technical editor would still change is phrasing, not content: "padrões de acesso mais planos" is a calque of "flatter access patterns" (PT would say "mais diretos"/"mais simples"), "pode ser necessário olhar mais fundo do que apenas o acesso equivalente" is stiff word-for-word English syntax ("ir além do acesso equivalente"), and "readout length" is rendered "comprimento de leitura" even though the cell it documents is `.duration` — a time quantity, so "duração da leitura" is the term a PT engineer would write. The unpluralized "dois qubit"/"subconjunto de qubit" reads awkwardly but stems from the kept-term glossary handled by the separate sweep, so it is not counted here.

examples.why: "mais planos" is a literal calque of "flatter"; in PT software prose the idiomatic contrast to nested/deep access is "mais diretos" or "mais simples". Meaning survives but it reads as MT.

examples.why: "comprimento" denotes spatial length; the quantity here is a time (the row maps to `.duration`). Not misleading given the code cell, but "duração da leitura" (or "tempo de leitura") is the conventional PT term.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — the example scenario (Fatima → `ml`, Ravi → `finance`, Amyra → ambos), the `quantum-computing.job.delete` custom rule, and the "não podem ser gerenciados até que aceitem o convite e façam login pelo menos uma vez" caveat all match the English exactly, and the informal "que você deseja convidar" register holds. editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no drift, no hallucination, no dropped caveat; the hedges survive ("might also support" → "maaari ding suportahan", "At minimum" → "Sa pinakamababa"), and the garbled English at line 47 is normalized cleanly without adding a claim. Terminology is correct and consistent (execution → pagpapatakbo in both the heading and both body uses; kahilingan for "requests"; backend/primitives/qubit/transpile correctly kept in English). The defects are three grammar/naturalness slips clustered in the opening paragraphs: "mapakinabangan ang nito userbase" puts the possessive in English word order (Tagalog requires "ang userbase nito") and is ungrammatical as written; "kailangan gumawa" is missing the linker ("kailangang gumawa"); and the relative clause "na sumusuporta ... at ibinabalik" switches from actor focus to object focus mid-coordination, where "at nagbabalik" is needed to agree with "na". None of these mislead a learner — they just read as unedited MT in an otherwise clean file.

examples.source: integrate their services into Qiskit and tap into its userbase
examples.suggested: i-integrate ang kanilang mga serbisyo sa Qiskit at mapakinabangan ang userbase nito
examples.translation: i-integrate ang kanilang mga serbisyo sa Qiskit at mapakinabangan ang nito userbase
examples.why: "ang nito userbase" is a direct calque of English possessive order and is ungrammatical in Tagalog; the enclitic pronoun "nito" must follow the noun it modifies. A native technical writer would never produce this.

examples.source: Doing so requires creating a package that supports requests for quantum compute resources and returns them to the user.
examples.suggested: Para magawa ito, kailangang gumawa ng package na sumusuporta sa mga kahilingan para sa quantum compute resources at nagbabalik ng mga ito sa user.
examples.translation: Para magawa ito, kailangan gumawa ng package na sumusuporta sa mga kahilingan para sa quantum compute resources at ibinabalik ang mga ito sa user.
examples.why: Two slips in one sentence: "kailangan gumawa" drops the required linker (-ng), and the coordinated relative clause shifts focus — "na sumusuporta" is actor-focus but "ibinabalik ang mga ito" is object-focus, so the second verb no longer attaches to "na package". Meaning is still recoverable, so this does not mislead.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no drift, no hallucination, no dropped caveats; the 1,000-test benchmarking claim, the "with or without noise" Aer description, the M3 "nominally nagko-converge sa O(1) hakbang" clause and the "walang sampling noise" parenthetical all survive intact, and the informal register holds (no po/opo). What a native technical editor would change is phrasing: "ang Qiskit SDK ay sino-subject sa benchmarking" (line 44) is an English verb crudely Tagalized where "ni-benchmark" / "sinusubok gamit ang benchmarking" is idiomatic; "Ang mga kakayahang ito ay nagtatayo sa matibay na pundasyon ng Qiskit ng mga kasangkapan" (line 48) is a word-order calque of "build upon Qiskit's performant foundation of tools" that leaves the genitive chain dangling, and "matibay" (sturdy) also flattens "performant". Two smaller slips: "nag-i-integrate sa isang workflow" softens "plug into a workflow" (addons are described elsewhere as pluggable, not integrated), and "naglulutas para sa mga corrected measurement probability" is a literal calque of "solves for". None of these would mislead a learner.

examples.source: the Qiskit SDK is benchmarked using over 1,000 tests developed by leading universities
examples.suggested: ni-benchmark ang Qiskit SDK gamit ang mahigit 1,000 test na binuo ng mga nangungunang unibersidad
examples.translation: ang Qiskit SDK ay sino-subject sa benchmarking gamit ang mahigit 1,000 na test na binuo ng mga nangungunang unibersidad
examples.why: "sino-subject" is a raw English verb given Tagalog aspect infixation — no native technical writer would produce it; the field already uses "i-benchmark" as the verb.

examples.source: These capabilities build upon Qiskit's performant foundation of tools for creating and running quantum algorithms.
examples.suggested: Nakasandig ang mga kakayahang ito sa mabilis at matatag na pundasyon ng mga kasangkapan ng Qiskit para sa paglikha at pagpapatakbo ng mga quantum algorithm.
examples.translation: Ang mga kakayahang ito ay nagtatayo sa matibay na pundasyon ng Qiskit ng mga kasangkapan para sa paglikha at pagpapatakbo ng mga quantum algorithm.
examples.why: Calqued English word order splits "pundasyon ... ng mga kasangkapan" across the possessor, and "nagtatayo sa" (erects on) is the wrong sense of "build upon"; "matibay" also loses the performance sense of "performant".

examples.source: Addons are modular software components that plug into a workflow to scale or design new quantum algorithms.
examples.suggested: ... na maisasaksak (plug-in) sa isang umiiral nang workflow
examples.translation: Ang mga addon ay mga modular na software component na nag-i-integrate sa isang workflow
examples.why: "nag-i-integrate" describes a merged component, while "plug into" is precisely the pluggable/modular property the sentence is teaching; the nuance of drop-in modularity is flattened.

examples.source: Benchmarking tests for quantum software might, for example, look at the speed and quality of building, manipulating, and transpiling circuits.
examples.suggested: Maaaring tingnan, halimbawa, ng mga benchmarking test para sa quantum software ang bilis at kalidad ng pagbuo, pag-manipula, at pag-transpile ng mga circuit.
examples.translation: Ang mga benchmarking test para sa quantum software ay maaaring, halimbawa, tingnan ang bilis at kalidad ng pagbuo, pag-manipula, at pag-transpile ng mga circuit.
examples.why: The mid-clause parenthetical "maaaring, halimbawa, tingnan" mirrors English comma placement and reads stilted in Tagalog, where the modal and verb are normally adjacent.

editor_note: No misleading content: the batch/session/job tradeoffs, the "QPU processes one job at a time but up to five classical jobs in parallel" fact, the "less than / more than one minute of QPU time" thresholds, the drift caveat ("dapat kang makakuha ng mas magandang resulta, ngunit ang device drift ay maaaring gawing mas masama ang mga kasunod na resulta"), and the PEA/PEC stale-noise-model caveat are all faithful, and the register is consistently informal (mo/iyong, no po/opo). What a native technical editor would still change: the concessive "While a QPU can process only one job at a time" is calqued as "Habang isang job lang ang kayang iproseso ng QPU" — "habang" is temporal in Tagalog, the contrastive sense needs "Samantalang"/"Bagaman"; step 2 of the variational flow renders "Evaluate the cost function" as "Suriin ang cost function" (analyze/inspect) rather than compute/evaluate, which slightly flattens the algorithm step; and two intensity qualifiers are dropped — "significantly faster than running them serially" becomes plain "mas mabilis kaysa sa paisa-isa", and "as tightly together as possible" / "as closely together as possible" both collapse to "nang magkakasabay". Also "learn the noise model" is rendered with the human-learning verb "matuto ng noise model" instead of an inferring/estimating verb.

examples.source: While a QPU can process only one job at a time, up to five classical jobs can be processed in parallel.
examples.suggested: Samantalang isang job lang ang kayang iprosesong sabay-sabay ng QPU, hanggang limang classical job ang maaaring iproseso nang parallel.
examples.translation: Habang isang job lang ang kayang iproseso ng QPU sa isang pagkakataon, hanggang limang classical job ang maaaring iproseso nang sabay.
examples.why: English 'while' here is contrastive, not temporal. Tagalog 'habang' reads strictly as 'during the time that', so the sentence lands as a time clause — a direct calque a native technical writer would render with 'samantalang' or 'bagaman'. Meaning is still recoverable, so MINOR.

examples.source: Evaluate the cost function on a QPU.
examples.suggested: I-evaluate (kalkulahin) ang cost function sa isang QPU.
examples.translation: Suriin ang cost function sa isang QPU.
examples.why: 'Suriin' means examine/analyze; in the variational loop step 2 is computing the value of the cost function, which the QPU then feeds to the classical optimizer. The reader can still follow the loop from steps 3-4, so this is a weakened rather than false rendering.

examples.source: Thus, running multiple jobs in a batch is significantly faster than running them serially.
examples.suggested: Kaya ang pagpapatakbo ng maraming job sa isang batch ay makabuluhang mas mabilis kaysa sa paisa-isa.
examples.translation: Kaya ang pagpapatakbo ng maraming job sa isang batch ay mas mabilis kaysa sa paisa-isa.
examples.why: 'significantly' is dropped, softening the main selling point of batch mode from a large speedup to a generic 'faster'. Same pattern at lines 24 and 72, where 'as tightly together as possible' / 'as closely together as possible' both flatten to plain 'nang magkakasabay', losing the 'as ... as possible' emphasis.

examples.source: you can learn the noise model once and apply it to subsequent jobs
examples.suggested: maaari mong tantiyahin/i-learn ang noise model nang isang beses at ilapat ito sa mga susunod na job
examples.translation: maaari kang matuto ng noise model nang isang beses at ilapat ito sa mga susunod na job
examples.why: 'matuto ng' is the intransitive human-learning verb ('you can learn/study'), whereas the source uses 'learn' in the machine-learning sense of characterizing the noise model once and reusing it. Recognizable in context (the link points to the noise-learning guide), hence MINOR.

editor_note: Faithful throughout: the Estimator caveat keeps both halves intact ("не пропонує реалізацій пом'якшення помилок вимірювання або вентилів «з коробки», оскільки backend-примітиви призначені для локального запуску на машині користувача"), the Sampler `memory` requirement and the BackendV2 conditional ("якщо він реалізує інтерфейс BackendV2") are preserved, terminology (примітив / провайдер / backend-примітив / вентилі) is consistent, and the informal register holds ("Ознайомся з документацією API").

No misleading content: the technically dense last 40% (ensemble_standard_error vs stds, twirling, ZNE regression weights, "Коли twirling не увімкнено, `stds` та `ensemble_standard_error` рівні") tracks the English claim-for-claim, and the informal "ти" convention holds throughout ("Зрозумій формат…", "групуй їх у тому ж PUB"). What a native editor would change: (1) the intro mis-parses the English "both the PUBs used as well as the runtime options" as a count — "залежить від обох PUB, використовуваних як вхідні дані" reads as "on both PUBs", where the correct construction is "як від використаних PUB, так і від опцій"; (2) "broadcasting" is rendered "правил трансляції NumPy" / "транслюваної форми" here, while the sibling guide job-limits.mdx uses "широкомовної передачі (broadcasting)" — within this file it is at least consistent; (3) several English-syntax calques survive: "виробляють додаткову інформацію" (for "produce", native: надають/дають), "візуальний контур структури даних" (for "visual outline", native: схематичний огляд), "де останній індекс — над об'єктами `Parameter`" (calque of "is over"); (4) "shot" is rendered "знімок" (кожен знімок виконання, кількість знімків) with no "(shots)" gloss on first use, unlike primitive-input-output.mdx and job-limits.mdx which gloss it — the corpus convention, but here the reader meets "снapshot"-flavoured wording cold next to $N_{shots}$.

examples.source: the results are returned in a format that is dependent on both the PUBs used as well as the runtime options specified from the primitive.
examples.suggested: результати повертаються у форматі, який залежить як від використаних PUB, так і від опцій середовища виконання, заданих для примітива.

examples.why: English "both X as well as Y" is a correlative conjunction, not a quantity; "від обох PUB" reads in Ukrainian as "on both (the two) PUBs", quietly implying a job has exactly two PUBs. Context still lists the two dependency factors, so it is confusing rather than false — but it is the one sentence in the file whose surface meaning differs from the source.

examples.source: you can think of each shot of the Estimator execution as providing a point estimate … $N_{shots}$ is the number of shots

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no drift, no hallucination, no dropped caveat: the kernel-restart warning ("Перезапуск Python-ядра призводить до втрати будь-яких результатів, збережених у пам'яті"), the three-month `created_after` window, and the `datetime.datetime` requirement all match the English exactly, and the informal "ти" register holds consistently ("щоб ти міг отримати їх пізніше", "використовуй метод"). Two purely stylistic slips a native technical editor would fix: "найнедавніші надіслані завдання" for "the most recently submitted jobs" is a superlative Ukrainian speakers do not form that way (natural: "останні надіслані завдання" / "найновіші завдання"), and "разом із енкодерами" violates the з/із euphony rule before a vowel ("з енкодерами"). Neither would mislead a learner.

examples.suggested: За замовчуванням він повертає останні надіслані завдання, але можна також фільтрувати за назвою бекенду, датою створення тощо.
examples.translation: За замовчуванням він повертає найнедавніші надіслані завдання, але можна також фільтрувати за назвою бекенду, датою створення тощо.
examples.why: "найнедавніші" is a superlative Ukrainian does not naturally form from "недавній"; it reads as calqued from "most recently". Native technical writing uses "останні надіслані завдання" or "найновіші завдання". Meaning is still clear, so MINOR.

examples.source: To do this, use Python's built-in JSON library with encoders from Qiskit Runtime.
examples.suggested: Для цього використовуй вбудовану бібліотеку JSON з Python разом з енкодерами Qiskit Runtime.
examples.translation: Для цього використовуй вбудовану бібліотеку JSON Python разом із енкодерами з Qiskit Runtime.
examples.why: "із енкодерами" breaks the з/із euphony rule (із is used before consonant clusters, not before a vowel), and the stacked genitive chain "бібліотеку JSON Python" is stiff. Cosmetic only — the instruction is unambiguous.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — the win/lose conditions ($a=b$ for three question pairs, $a\neq b$ for $(1,1)$), the 3/4 classical bound, the 0.85 quantum value, Tsirelson (متراجحة تسيريلسون) and the local-hidden-variable remark all match the English, and the case-by-case analysis carries no inverted condition or swapped quantity. The defects are terminological and stylistic: "tensor product" is rendered *الحاصل التنسيقي* ("coordinative product") instead of the conventional الجداء/حاصل الضرب التنسوري — recognizable next to the ⊗ symbol but not the field's term; and "parameterizing rotations" becomes "معاملتها" ("treating them"), which drops the parameterization idea rather than reversing it. On top of that there are agreement slips ("تديرها *حَكَم*" should be يديرها; "الأسسَين التي" is a malformed dual for الأساسين اللذين) and a run of English calques — "بديلًا" used adverbially for "alternatively" (lines 121, 223, 258), "يحدث أن تكون" for "happens to be", "لا نستطيع التحسين على هذا" for "can't do better", "تجاوز الفوز ... 75% من الوقت". None of these would mislead a learner; a native technical editor would still rewrite them.

examples.source: If we compute the inner product of the *tensor product* of any two of these vectors with the |φ+⟩ state
examples.suggested: إذا حسبنا الضرب الداخلي لـ*الجداء التنسوري* لأي متجهين من هذه المتجهات مع الحالة |φ+⟩
examples.translation: إذا حسبنا الحاصل الداخلي لـ*الحاصل التنسيقي* لأي متجهين من هذه المتجهات مع حالة |φ+⟩
examples.why: ‘تنسيقي’ means coordinative/organizational, not tensorial; the standard Arabic rendering is تنسوري (or الضرب الموتري). Recoverable from the adjacent ⊗ symbol, so imperfect rather than false, but it is not the field's term.

examples.source: If we follow a standard convention for naming and parameterizing rotations of various forms, we have U_θ = R_y(−2θ)
examples.suggested: وباتباع الاصطلاح القياسي في تسمية الدورانات المختلفة وتوصيفها بمعاملات، يكون U_θ = R_y(-2θ)
examples.translation: باتباع اصطلاح قياسي لتسمية الدورانات ومعاملتها بأشكال متنوعة، لدينا U_θ = R_y(-2θ)
examples.why: ‘معاملتها’ reads as ‘treating them’, so the parameterization — the whole point of the R_y(θ) convention that follows — is lost, and ‘بأشكال متنوعة’ is attached to the verb instead of to ‘rotations of various forms’.

examples.source: The game is run by a *referee*, who behaves according to strict guidelines that are known to Alice and Bob.
examples.suggested: يديرها *حَكَم* يلتزم بمبادئ توجيهية صارمة معروفة لأليس وبوب.
examples.translation: تديرها *حَكَم* يلتزم بمبادئ توجيهية صارمة معروفة لدى أليس وبوب.
examples.why: Gender agreement error: the subject حَكَم is masculine (confirmed by the following يلتزم), so the verb must be يديرها, not تديرها.

examples.source: This happens to be the *optimal* winning probability for quantum strategies. That is, we can't do any better than this
examples.suggested: وتصادف أن تكون هذه هي احتمالية الفوز *المثلى* للاستراتيجيات الكمية؛ أي لا يمكننا تحقيق ما هو أفضل من ذلك
examples.translation: يحدث أن تكون هذه احتمالية الفوز *المثلى* للاستراتيجيات الكمية. أي أننا لا نستطيع التحسين على هذا
examples.why: Two word-for-word calques in consecutive sentences: ‘يحدث أن تكون’ for ‘happens to be’ and ‘التحسين على هذا’ for ‘do better than this’; a native technical writer would never phrase either that way.

examples.source: These equations can be connected to the figures above by imagining that we superimpose the bases chosen by Alice and Bob.
examples.suggested: يمكن ربط هذه المعادلات بالأشكال أعلاه بتخيّل تراكب الأساسين اللذين اختارهما أليس وبوب.
examples.translation: يمكن ربط هذه المعادلات بالأشكال أعلاه بتخيّل دمج الأسسَين التي اختارهما أليس وبوب.
examples.why: ‘الأسسَين’ welds a broken plural onto a dual ending and is followed by the feminine-singular relative التي instead of اللذين; ‘دمج’ (merge) also weakens ‘superimpose’, which is تراكب — the figure shows the two bases overlaid, not fused.

editor_note: The core term "observable" is rendered throughout as "متغيّر" (= variable / variant), roughly ten times (lines 50, 162, 205, 256, 293, 310, 329, 348, 464), which teaches a false concept: an observable is a Hermitian operator, not a variable, and this lesson is entirely about estimating expectation values of one. The damage is compounded because "متغيّر" is simultaneously the file's word for "variant" — line 205 reads "هو متغيّر من VQE ... أول k قيم ذاتية لمتغيّر Ĥ", using the same word for "variant of VQE" and for "observable Ĥ" in one sentence, so the concept becomes unidentifiable; line 297 ("الحالات الذاتية لمتغيّر ما، أو مؤثر هيرميتي") makes the contradiction explicit, and line 464 tells the learner to think of this "متغيّر" as the Hamiltonian of a system. Correct renderings would be "مؤثر قابل للرصد" / "الكمية المرصودة". Secondary: "excited state" is consistently "حالة متحمِّسة" (= enthusiastic state) instead of the standard "حالة مثارة" (lines 372, 381, 430, 464, 472); "Deflation" in VQD is "الانحراف" (= deviation) rather than a deflation/reduction sense; and there are calques such as "سنستدعي الخطوات" for "call out the steps" (line 24) and "الحد الأدنى العالمي" for "global minimum" (line 608).

examples.source: SSVQE is a variant of VQE that allows obtaining the first $k$ eigenvalues of an observable $\hat{H}$
examples.suggested: هو صيغة مختلفة من VQE تتيح الحصول على أول $k$ قيم ذاتية لمؤثر قابل للرصد $\hat{H}$
examples.translation: هو متغيّر من VQE يتيح الحصول على أول $k$ قيم ذاتية لمتغيّر $\hat{H}$
examples.why: The same word متغيّر carries "variant" and "observable" inside one sentence; the second use also mislabels a Hermitian operator as a "variable", so the learner cannot identify what Ĥ actually is.

examples.source: We will introduce an observable to be estimated. ... It may be helpful to think of this observable as the Hamiltonian of a system that can have excited states
examples.suggested: سنُدخل مؤثرًا قابلًا للرصد لتقديره. ... قد يكون من المفيد التفكير في هذا المؤثر على أنه هاملتوني لنظام يمكن أن تكون له حالات مثارة
examples.translation: سنُدخل متغيّرًا للتقدير. ... قد يكون من المفيد التفكير في هذا المتغيّر على أنه هاملتوني لنظام يمكن أن تكون له حالات متحمِّسة
examples.why: Teaches that a Hamiltonian is a "variable"; and "متحمِّسة" (enthusiastic) is not the physics term for an excited state, which is "مثارة".

examples.source: Here's the example for the following observable: ... and we will apply the corresponding layout to the observable.
examples.suggested: إليك المثال للمؤثر القابل للرصد التالي: ... ونُطبّق التخطيط المقابل على المؤثر القابل للرصد.
examples.translation: إليك المثال للمتغير التالي: ... ونُطبّق التخطيط المقابل على المتغير.
examples.why: A Pauli operator O₁ = 2II − 2XX + 3YY − 3ZZ is introduced as "the following variable", and "applying a layout to a variable" is meaningless — layouts apply to operators/circuits.

examples.source: The Qiskit patterns framework applies to all these algorithms - but we will explicitly call out the steps only in the first example.
examples.suggested: ... غير أننا سنشير إلى الخطوات صراحةً في المثال الأول فقط.
examples.translation: يسري إطار أنماط Qiskit على جميع هذه الخوارزميات — غير أننا سنستدعي الخطوات صراحةً في المثال الأول فقط.
examples.why: "نستدعي" means invoke/summon (and reads as a function call in a programming text); "call out" here means point out, so the calque is stiff and mildly confusing in a Qiskit context.

editor_note: Faithful and idiomatic across the file's short prose; informal register holds ("أنك قد حفظت بيانات اعتمادك"، "اتّبع التعليمات"), and "quantum-centric supercomputing" is rendered with the correct conventional term "الحوسبة الفائقة المتمحورة حول الكم" with no drift in the credentials caveat or the Next-steps recommendation.

No semantic drift found: every quantitative claim, caveat and conditional survives intact (128 filas / 14 características / 15.° elemento, 90 entrenamiento + 30 prueba, 0,90^10 ≈ 35%, "profundidad de dos qubits de más de 100 ... antes de la transpilación", $(1-p)^N$, "reducir el número de cálculos a la mitad"), the informal "tú" holds throughout ("Puedes construir", "Ten en cuenta", "Te animamos a explorar"), and core terms are consistent (qubit, puertas, backend, pass manager, mapa de características, matriz kernel). The one term worth changing is "overlap", rendered as "superposición" ("circuito de superposición (overlap)", "su superposición es bastante grande en comparación con la superposición máxima") — in a quantum text "superposición" is the loaded word for *superposition*, and "solapamiento" (or "traslape") is the conventional rendering for overlap; the parenthetical gloss at first use keeps it recognizable, so it does not mislead, but it is the top fix. Remaining nits are stylistic: "es un criterio eliminatorio" for "is a non-starter", "tomar el circuito más superficial" for "the shallowest circuit" (native: "el circuito de menor profundidad"), "circuito auto-construido" / "no es practicable" as calques, "aún antes de la transpilación" (should be unaccented "aun"), and an added helper sentence ("Lee las siguientes preguntas, piensa en las respuestas y luego haz clic en los triángulos...") that has no source counterpart — benign, it accompanies the Accordion→<details> conversion.

examples.source: their overlap is fairly large compared to the maximum overlap (which would be 1.0) / We will construct an overlap circuit / we transpile the unitary overlap circuit 20 times
examples.suggested: su solapamiento es bastante grande en comparación con el solapamiento máximo (que sería 1,0) / Creamos un circuito de solapamiento (overlap) / el circuito de solapamiento unitario
examples.translation: su superposición es bastante grande en comparación con la superposición máxima (que sería 1,0) / Creamos un circuito de superposición (overlap) / transpilamos el circuito de superposición unitaria 20 veces
examples.why: "superposición" is the established Spanish term for quantum *superposition*, a different concept; using it for "overlap" in a quantum-computing lesson invites confusion. Context and the one-time "(overlap)" gloss keep it recognizable, so MINOR, but "solapamiento" is the conventional domain rendering.

examples.source: But a two-qubit depth of more than 100, even before transpilation is a non-starter.
examples.suggested: Pero una profundidad de dos qubits superior a 100, aun antes de la transpilación, es inviable de entrada.
examples.translation: Pero una profundidad de dos qubits de más de 100, aún antes de la transpilación, es un criterio eliminatorio.
examples.why: "criterio eliminatorio" (an elimination criterion, sports/exam register) is not how a Spanish technical writer renders "non-starter"; also "aún" should be the unaccented "aun" (= 'incluso') here.

examples.source: It is often useful to transpile a few times and take the shallowest circuit.
examples.suggested: A menudo conviene transpilar varias veces y quedarse con el circuito de menor profundidad.
examples.translation: A menudo tiene sentido transpilar varias veces y tomar el circuito más superficial.
examples.why: "más superficial" is a literal calque of "shallowest"; in circuit-depth discussion Spanish uses "de menor profundidad" — the file itself already says "el circuito con la menor profundidad" in the Resumen, so this is also an internal inconsistency.

examples.source: Now that we have a kernel matrix and a similarly formatted test_matrix from quantum kernel methods
examples.suggested: Ahora que tenemos una matriz kernel y una test_matrix con el mismo formato, obtenidas mediante métodos de kernel cuántico
examples.translation: Dado que ahora tenemos una matriz kernel y una test_matrix formateada correspondiente a partir de métodos de kernel cuántico
examples.why: "formateada correspondiente" is a stiff, ambiguous rendering of "similarly formatted"; the trailing "a partir de" also detaches from its verb, making the sentence read as machine output rather than authored prose.

examples.source: (no counterpart in the English source)
examples.suggested: (optional) keep, but note it is translator-added scaffolding for the <details> widget
examples.translation: Lee las siguientes preguntas, piensa en las respuestas y luego haz clic en los triángulos para ver las soluciones.
examples.why: An added instructional sentence with no source counterpart. Harmless and consistent with the Accordion→<details> conversion, but it is content the English does not have; flagging for the record, not as a defect that misleads.

editor_note: Prose is fluent, informal-"tú" throughout, and domain terms are sound (qubits, puertas de 2 qubits, diafonía for crosstalk, entrelazamiento, tolerantes a fallos, mitigación de errores); the source's "Rolf Launduer" typo is even silently corrected to "Rolf Landauer". Nothing misleads, but a native editor would still fix several small fidelity slips: the qualifier in "which are not exact and don't all agree in their predictions" is lost ("que no son exactos y no coinciden en sus predicciones" — asserts they never agree); the forward-reference sentence "We'll summarize the current state of the technology in a section below." is dropped entirely from the "Computación cuántica en la práctica" section; "a back-and-forth interaction with classical computing" flattens to plain "una interacción con la computación clásica", losing the ping-pong image the next sentence depends on; and "the prediction of eclipses and tides" gains an unsourced "eclipses solares y lunares". Terminology-wise the key concept is split within the file: "*utilidad*" and "demostrar *utilidad*" early on vs. the untranslated "*Quantum Utility*" in the same section heading and in later sentences.

examples.source: different simulation methods (which are not exact and don't all agree in their predictions)
examples.suggested: ...(que no son exactos y que no todos coinciden en sus predicciones)
examples.translation: diferentes métodos de simulación (que no son exactos y no coinciden en sus predicciones)
examples.why: "don't all agree" (some disagree) is strengthened to "no coinciden" (none agree); the dropped quantifier changes the claim about the state of classical simulation methods.

examples.source: We'll summarize the current state of the technology in a section below.
examples.suggested: Resumiremos el estado actual de la tecnología en una sección más abajo.
examples.translation: (omitted — the paragraph ends at "pero hemos recorrido un largo camino desde entonces.")
examples.why: A whole source sentence is missing; the reader loses the forward pointer to the later "Estado de la tecnología" section.

examples.source: As this happens we're likely to see a back-and-forth interaction with classical computing:
examples.suggested: ...probablemente veremos una interacción de ida y vuelta con la computación clásica:
examples.translation: Cuando eso suceda, probablemente veremos una interacción con la computación clásica:
examples.why: "back-and-forth" is the whole point of the following sentence (demo, response, another turn, repeat); without it the setup no longer prepares the example.

examples.source: quantum utility / demonstrate *utility*
examples.suggested: Pick one rendering (e.g. *utilidad cuántica*) and use it in the heading and all body mentions.
examples.translation: heading "### Quantum Utility", "demostrar *utilidad*" (l.27), "conocido como *Quantum Utility*" (l.35), "no podían demostrar Quantum Utility" (l.62)
examples.why: The same central concept appears both translated and untranslated within one file, so the learner cannot tell whether "utilidad" and "Quantum Utility" are the same notion.

examples.source: figuring out how best to do this represents a challenge for superconducting qubit circuits
examples.suggested: averiguar cuál es la mejor forma de hacerlo representa un reto para los circuitos de qubits superconductores
examples.translation: el desafío de cómo hacerlo mejor representa un desafío para los circuitos de qubits superconductores
examples.why: "el desafío ... representa un desafío" is a redundant echo no native technical writer would leave, and "cómo hacerlo mejor" reads as "how to do it better" rather than "how best to do it".

editor_note: No semantic drift or hallucination: every claim, list item and caveat matches the English (course list, exam/badge flow, Credly privacy notice all faithful). The defects are register and phrasing. The file is written in formal "usted" throughout ("Aprenda sobre estados cuánticos", "Para obtener su insignia... tome el examen", "será notificado"), against the project's informal-"tú" convention, and then slips into "tú" for one sentence ("Recibirás una notificación por correo electrónico de Credly"), so the register is also internally inconsistent. Terminology-wise, three distinct English course titles — "Basics of", "Fundamentals of", "Foundations of" — all collapse to "Fundamentos de", flattening the series' deliberate naming ladder; and "single and multiple systems" becomes "sistemas únicos y múltiples", where "únicos" reads as "unique" rather than "individual/de un solo sistema". Two calqued constructions remain stiff: "adecuado para aquellos en o más allá de un nivel universitario avanzado" and "Este examen está destinado a ser tomado después de leer las lecciones". None of these would teach a learner anything false.

examples.source: Learn about quantum states... / take the exam at IBM Training... you will be notified by Credly
examples.suggested: Aprende sobre estados cuánticos... / haz el examen en IBM Training... Recibirás una notificación...
examples.translation: Aprenda sobre estados cuánticos... / tome el examen en IBM Training... Recibirás una notificación por correo electrónico de Credly
examples.why: The page is formal usted almost everywhere (Aprenda, su insignia, tome, será notificado) against the informal-tú convention, and then switches to tú for one sentence inside the same section, so the voice is inconsistent as well as formal.

examples.source: Basics of quantum information ... Fundamentals of quantum algorithms ... Foundations of quantum error correction
examples.suggested: Conceptos básicos de la información cuántica ... Fundamentos de los algoritmos cuánticos ... Bases de la corrección de errores cuánticos
examples.translation: Fundamentos de información cuántica ... Fundamentos de algoritmos cuánticos ... Fundamentos de corrección de errores cuánticos
examples.why: Three deliberately different English titles in the same series collapse onto one Spanish word, erasing the Basics→Fundamentals→Foundations progression the course list is meant to convey.

examples.source: a description of quantum information for both single and multiple systems
examples.suggested: una descripción de la información cuántica tanto para sistemas individuales como para sistemas múltiples
examples.translation: una descripción de la información cuántica para sistemas únicos y múltiples
examples.why: "únicos" reads as "unique" rather than "a single system"; the intended single-system vs multiple-system contrast is the core structure of the course and should be explicit ("individuales", plus "tanto... como" for "both").

examples.source: suitable for those at or beyond an advanced undergraduate level / This exam is intended to be taken after reading the lessons in this course
examples.suggested: apropiado para quienes tengan un nivel de grado avanzado o superior / Conviene hacer el examen después de leer las lecciones del curso
examples.translation: adecuado para aquellos en o más allá de un nivel universitario avanzado / Este examen está destinado a ser tomado después de leer las lecciones de este curso
examples.why: Both are word-order calques from English; "en o más allá de" and the passive "está destinado a ser tomado" are constructions no Spanish technical writer would produce, and "universitario" alone loses the undergraduate/grado distinction.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no drift, no dropped caveats, no hallucination; chemistry terminology is strong and consistent (opérateurs mono-électroniques / énergies bi-électroniques, décomposition de faible rang, groupe de symétrie ponctuelle, représentation irréductible) and the informal "tu" convention holds everywhere. Three wording slips a native technical editor would fix: (1) PySCF's API call kernel() is translated literally as « Le noyau de celui-ci (E, ci-dessous) », and in a sentence that goes on to mention « la répulsion nucléaire » the French « noyau » reads as *atomic nucleus* rather than the method name — the term should stay "kernel" like the other API names (scf, mcscf, ao2mo, ncas) already kept in this file. (2) « C'est le contraire des hamiltoniens utilisés dans Qiskit » overstates the English "This is in contrast to…" — Qiskit uses a different display convention, not the opposite one. (3) « les qubits 0 et 1 étant affectés par l'opérateur identité » renders "acted on by" as "affected by", awkward since the identity precisely does not affect those qubits; « sur lesquels agit l'opérateur identité » is the domain-standard phrasing. Minor stiffness also in « un certain mapping spécifique » (calque of "some mapping").

examples.source: The kernel of this (E, below) is the total energy, including nuclear repulsion and molecular orbitals.
examples.suggested: Le `kernel` de celui-ci (E, ci-dessous) est l'énergie totale, incluant la répulsion nucléaire et les orbitales moléculaires.
examples.translation: Le noyau de celui-ci (E, ci-dessous) est l'énergie totale, incluant la répulsion nucléaire et les orbitales moléculaires.
examples.why: 'kernel' here is the PySCF API method (mf.kernel()), a code identifier. Rendering it as « noyau » in a quantum-chemistry sentence that immediately mentions « la répulsion nucléaire » invites the reader to parse it as the atomic nucleus. The adjacent code block makes it recoverable, so this is minor, but it should be kept in English like the other API names already are.

examples.source: This is in contrast to Hamiltonians used in Qiskit, which would write the term `[Z2 Z3]` as `ZZII`
examples.suggested: Cela contraste avec les hamiltoniens utilisés dans Qiskit, qui écriraient le terme `[Z2 Z3]` sous la forme `ZZII`
examples.translation: C'est le contraire des hamiltoniens utilisés dans Qiskit, qui écriraient le terme `[Z2 Z3]` sous la forme `ZZII`
examples.why: 'in contrast to' compares two differing conventions; « c'est le contraire de » asserts they are opposites. Qiskit's convention is not the inverse of OpenFermion's — it simply spells out identities and drops the indices. The practical instruction and the `ZZII` example are intact, so this stays MINOR rather than misleading.

examples.source: (qubits 0 and 1 being acting on by the identity operator, qubits 2 and 3 being acted on by the Z operator, ordered with qubit 0 furthest to the right)
examples.suggested: (l'opérateur identité agissant sur les qubits 0 et 1, l'opérateur Z agissant sur les qubits 2 et 3, ordonnés avec le qubit 0 à l'extrême droite)
examples.translation: (les qubits 0 et 1 étant affectés par l'opérateur identité, les qubits 2 et 3 étant affectés par l'opérateur Z, ordonnés avec le qubit 0 à l'extrême droite)
examples.why: 'acted on by' is « sur lesquels agit » in French operator language; « affectés par » means 'affected by', which is odd precisely because the identity operator leaves those qubits unaffected. Operator assignment and qubit ordering are both correct, so the learner still reads the label correctly — a fluency/terminology fix, not a meaning error.

editor_note: Substance is faithful and the core terminology is correct and consistent throughout (générateurs de stabilisateurs, case = tile, sommet = vertex, boucle fermée, couplage parfait de poids minimum, espace de code, code stabilisateur [[2L²,2,L]]). Three real gaps: (a) the EN disambiguating gloss before the loop taxonomy — "Here, a 'horizontal/vertical lattice line' means a full row/column of qubits in the periodic lattice (not the line segments of the loop of qubits affected by the X error)" — is absent from the FR, as is the "since each lattice line crosses the closed loop once in and once out" justification in item 1, so the FR states the classification without the clarification and the reason the example belongs to category 1; (b) "doesn't need to involve too many qubits" becomes "ne doit pas impliquer trop de qubits", turning a benefit into a prohibition; (c) "quantum low-density parity check code" is rendered "code de contrôle de parité à faible densité quantique", where "quantique" reads as attached to "densité". Also one calqued English sentence frame ("Peut-être plus probable, selon le modèle de bruit, est qu'un syndrome…") and one formal-register slip ("Notez que"). None of these teaches a false concept — the correct even/odd-per-lattice-line criterion is restated correctly a few lines later — so this stays MINOR.

examples.source: In particular, the different types of loops can be characterized as follows. Here, a 'horizontal/vertical lattice line' means a full row/column of qubits in the periodic lattice (not the line segments of the loop of qubits affected by the X error). … The example shown above falls into this category, since each lattice line crosses the closed loop of errors once, say crossing into the closed loop, and once crossing back out of the closed loop of errors.
examples.suggested: En particulier, les différents types de boucles peuvent être caractérisés comme suit. editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no inverted conditions, no swapped quantities, no hallucinated claims; the disjoint-lattice setup, the CZ-within-chip / ECR-between-chip distinction, the arrow-direction control/target explanation and the SWAP-insertion reason for the gate-count inflation all survive intact, and register is consistent plain desu/masu with no keigo. Three editor-level slips: (1) in the BackendV2 bullet list, "a description of the constraints of the backend" is fused into the pseudo-API coinage 「BackendConstraintの記述」, which reads like a nonexistent Qiskit class rather than 「Backendの制約の記述」; (2) qubit is rendered two ways inside a single sentence — 「BackendのQubit配置や、Backendの量子ビット上での回路のレイアウト」 — and the split recurs (各Qubit / 2量子ビットゲート) across the file; (3) plot_circuit_layout is said to 「…Qubitと2量子ビットチャネルを指定します」, a literal calque of the source's loose "specify" that suggests the tool designates the qubits rather than displays which ones were used (示します/確認できます). Also, in 「…必要な情報をすべて含んでおり、制約に従って回路を最適化できます」 the elided subject reads as the backend class rather than the transpiler. None of these would leave a learner with a false idea of the mechanism.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no drift, no hallucination, no dropped caveat: the discard condition ("2 つの測定が期待通りのビット反転を確認できない場合…そのショットを破棄します"), the conservative bitwise-AND explanation ("node と edge の両方の戦略でパスしたショットのみを保持"), and the whole closing "not a complete solution / increased sampling overhead / broader strategy" paragraph all track the English exactly, and ポスト選択 / エラー緩和 / トランスパイル are used consistently. What a native technical editor would still change are four wording choices: "fractional gates" is calqued as 分数ゲート where the field writes フラクショナル・ゲート; "near-term (quantum hardware)" becomes 近期の, a Sino-calque that reads as "recent" rather than 近未来／短期的な; "probabilistic error cancellation" is rendered 確率的エラー消去, where 消去 suggests erasure rather than cancellation (usual: 確率的エラーキャンセレーション／誤り相殺); and "post-processing step" is ポスト処理ステップ instead of the standard 後処理. All are recognizable and none would teach a false concept.

editor_note: Faithful and natural throughout: the intro correctly keeps both branches of the EN advice (結果をファイルに保存／IBM Quantum から過去のジョブの結果を取得 → 次のセッションで前回の続きから作業を再開), "filter jobs by backend name, creation date" → バックエンド名や作成日などでフィルタリング, and "load this array from disk in a separate kernel" → 別のカーネルでこの配列をディスクから読み込む; terminology (ジョブ／バックエンド／カーネル／エンコーダー) is consistent and the desu/masu register holds with no keigo.

Faithful and natural throughout; the error-ordering claim survives intact ("os erros de leitura tendem a ser maiores do que os da operação de 2 qubits, que por sua vez tendem a ser maiores do que os da operação de 1 qubit"), and terminology is correct and consistent (coupling map → "mapa de acoplamento", heavy-hex lattice → "rede heavy-hex", entangling gate → "porta de entrelaçamento de 2 qubits", median → "mediana dos tempos T1/T2"); Backend/Target/qubit kept in English as the field does, informal "você" register holds.

The translation is faithful on every load-bearing claim — the NYC tourist analogy for Quantum Volume, the four metrics (escala/qualidade/velocidade/fidelidade de camada), the Gross-code numbers (12 qubits lógicos, ~um milhão de ciclos, 288 qubits), the Starling figures (100 milhões de portas quânticas em 200 qubits lógicos) and the 2026/2029 dates all match, and core terminology (qubit, portas quânticas, valor esperado, mitigação de erros, taxa de erro, Volume Quântico) is correct and consistent with informal "você" throughout. What a native technical editor would change: "patterned on a silicon substrate" became "materiais supercondutores padrão em um substrato de silício", where "patterned" was read as the noun "padrão" — the sentence now claims the materials are "standard" and loses the lithographic-patterning idea (should be "padronizados/litografados sobre um substrato de silício"). "Quantum-centric supercomputing" is calqued word-order-first as "supercomputação quântica centrada" / heading "Supercomputadores quânticos centrados", which reads as "centered quantum supercomputers" rather than "centrada em quântica"; the concept survives only because the surrounding paragraph explains it. Smaller slips: "single photons of light" → "fótons de luz únicos" (should be "fótons individuais de luz"), the dropped qualifier "at one time" in "foi chamado de 'desafio 100x100'", and the Ising analogy flattened by rendering both "two-choice systems" and "two-state qubits" as "de dois estados", which makes "se parecem muito com os qubits de dois estados" tautological. None of these would make a learner believe something false about quantum computing, so this is not a FAIL.

examples.suggested: supercomputação centrada em quântica / Supercomputadores centrados em quântica
examples.translation: supercomputação quântica centrada / Supercomputadores quânticos centrados
examples.why: Word-order calque: the adjective "centrada" ends up modifying the supercomputing rather than expressing "centered on quantum", producing the odd "centered quantum supercomputers"; recognizable only from context.

examples.source: a lattice of interacting quantum two-choice systems ... These systems look a lot like the two-state qubits
examples.suggested: sistemas quânticos quânticos de duas escolhas ... se parecem muito com os qubits de dois estados
examples.translation: uma rede de sistemas quânticos de dois estados interagentes ... Esses sistemas se parecem muito com os qubits de dois estados
examples.why: English deliberately says "two-choice" for the Ising spins and "two-state" for qubits so the resemblance is a non-trivial observation; collapsing both to "de dois estados" makes the comparison tautological and flattens the intuition.

examples.source: was at one time called the "100x100 challenge"
examples.suggested: foi um dia chamado de "desafio 100x100"
examples.translation: foi chamado de "desafio 100x100"
examples.why: The qualifier "at one time" is dropped, so the reader loses the signal that the name is historical and has since been superseded by the 5k framing.

examples.source: photonic qubits, which are made from single photons of light
examples.suggested: qubits fotônicos, feitos de fótons individuais de luz
examples.translation: qubits fotônicos, que são feitos de fótons de luz únicos
examples.why: "fótons de luz únicos" is a calqued adjective placement that reads as "unique photons"; a native technical writer would write "fótons individuais".

editor_note: No semantic inversions, swapped quantities or hallucinations: parity logic (par/ímpar), the $2L^2$/$2$/$L$ parameters, the $[[2L^2,2,L]]$ statement, the "abaixo de uma taxa de ruído de aproximadamente 10\%" claim and the break-even paragraph all track the English exactly, and the informal "você" register holds. The real defect is in the loop-classification block (PT lines 143–147): the translation drops the English clarifier defining what a "horizontal/vertical lattice line" means ("a full row/column of qubits in the periodic lattice (not the line segments of the loop of qubits affected by the X error)") AND the justification clause in item 1 ("since each lattice line crosses the closed loop of errors once… and once crossing back out"), so the PT asserts the categories without explaining why the example belongs to category 1 — pedagogical flattening, not a false statement. Smaller slips: the same English phrase "wrap around the periodic boundaries" is rendered two different ways in adjacent sentences ("atravessam" then "contornam", PT lines 61–62), and "Such a loop of $X$ errors" becomes "Uma cadeia de erros como essa" (PT line 153) in a passage that has just been carefully distinguishing cadeias-com-extremidades from laços fechados.

examples.source: In particular, the different types of loops can be characterized as follows. Here, a 'horizontal/vertical lattice line' means a full row/column of qubits in the periodic lattice (not the line segments of the loop of qubits affected by the X error).
examples.suggested: Em particular, os diferentes tipos de laços podem ser caracterizados da seguinte forma. Aqui, uma "linha horizontal/vertical da malha" significa uma linha/coluna completa de qubits na malha periódica (e não os segmentos de reta do laço de qubits afetados pelo erro X).
examples.translation: Em particular, os diferentes tipos de laços podem ser caracterizados da seguinte forma.
examples.why: The English adds this sentence specifically to block a natural misreading of "lattice line"; the PT omits it entirely, so the reader of items 1 and 2 has no definition of the term the whole classification hinges on. Nothing false is asserted, but the disambiguation the author deliberately supplied is gone.

examples.source: The example shown above falls into this category, since each lattice line crosses the closed loop of errors once, say crossing into the closed loop, and once crossing back out of the closed loop of errors.
examples.suggested: O exemplo mostrado acima se enquadra nessa categoria, pois cada linha da malha cruza o laço fechado de erros uma vez ao entrar no laço e outra vez ao sair dele.
examples.translation: (O exemplo mostrado acima se enquadra nessa categoria.)
examples.why: The reason the example is category-1 (each lattice line crosses in and back out, hence an even count) is the whole intuition of the parity argument. The PT keeps only the bare claim in parentheses, so the learner is told the classification but not why it holds.

examples.source: Notice that the stabilizer generators that wrap around the periodic boundaries are included. These generators that wrap around the periodic boundaries are not special…
examples.translation: Observe que os geradores do estabilizador que atravessam as fronteiras periódicas estão incluídos. Esses geradores que contornam as fronteiras periódicas não são especiais…
examples.why: The identical English phrase "wrap around the periodic boundaries" is rendered "atravessam" and then "contornam" in back-to-back sentences; since the second sentence explicitly refers back to the first ("Esses geradores…"), the shift makes it read as if two different kinds of generator were being discussed. Pick one rendering (e.g. "contornam") and use it in both.

editor_note: The translation is overall faithful and readable, but one sentence destroys a technical condition: the caveat on correcting multiple Z errors, "as long as at most one block experiences an odd number of them", is rendered as "basta't kahit isang bloke lamang ang nakakaranas ng kakaibang bilang ng mga ito" (line 170) — "kakaiba" is the false-friend "odd = strange/weird", not the parity sense (gansal / di-pantay). The learner is left with a meaningless "a strange number of them" and cannot recover the parity rule that actually governs when the Shor code still corrects multiple Z errors. Secondary problems: line 190 opens with the non-word "Iniitiwa" where "Itinatama/Naitutuwid" is meant (EN "The Shor code corrects any Pauli error"), line 191 renders "we're assuming" as "inaasahan natin" (= we expect) instead of "ipinapalagay natin", and line 228 leaves the English "o thereabouts" untranslated. Also, "at most one X error" is repeatedly rendered as "kahit isang X error lamang" (lines 70, 114, 194), which reads closer to "even just one" than to the intended upper bound.

examples.source: or multiple $Z$ errors (as long as at most one block experiences an odd number of them)
examples.suggested: o maraming $Z$ error (basta't hindi hihigit sa isang bloke ang nakakaranas ng gansal (odd) na bilang ng mga ito)
examples.translation: o maraming $Z$ error (basta't kahit isang bloke lamang ang nakakaranas ng kakaibang bilang ng mga ito)
examples.why: 'odd number' (parity) is translated as 'kakaibang bilang' = 'a strange/unusual number'. The parity condition — the whole reason a block with an even number of Z errors is harmless — vanishes, and the learner is given a condition that cannot be applied or verified.

examples.source: The Shor code corrects any Pauli error on a single qubit, including a $Y$ error of course, but it doesn't properly correct two or more $Y$ errors.
examples.suggested: Naitatama ng Shor code ang anumang Pauli error sa iisang qubit, ...
examples.translation: Iniitiwa ng Shor code ang anumang Pauli error sa iisang qubit, kabilang ang isang $Y$ error siyempre, ngunit hindi nito naitutuwid nang wasto ang dalawa o higit pang mga $Y$ error.
examples.why: 'Iniitiwa' is not a Tagalog word; the main verb of the paragraph's key claim is garbled. The same sentence later uses the correct 'naitutuwid', so the file even contradicts itself on the verb.

examples.source: In particular, if there is at most one $X$ error on the nine qubits of the encoding, this error will be detected and corrected by this procedure.
examples.suggested: Sa partikular, kung hindi hihigit sa isang $X$ error ang mayroon sa siyam na qubit ng encoding, ...
examples.translation: Sa partikular, kung may kahit isang $X$ error lamang sa siyam na qubit ng encoding, ang error na ito ay dide-detect at itatama ng pamamaraang ito.
examples.why: 'kahit isang ... lamang' reads as 'even just one' rather than the upper bound 'at most one'. The guarantee only holds under the bound, so the softened phrasing weakens a load-bearing condition; it recurs three times in the file.

examples.source: As an aside, here we see an example of *degeneracy* in a quantum error-correcting code
examples.suggested: Bilang isang panabing puna, dito ay nakikita natin ang isang halimbawa ng *degeneracy* ...
examples.translation: Bilang isang paalala, dito ay nakikita natin ang isang halimbawa ng *degeneracy* sa isang quantum error-correcting code
examples.why: 'paalala' means 'reminder', implying the point was made before; 'As an aside' introduces a new side remark. Minor, but it misdirects the reader about the status of the degeneracy observation.

examples.source: Three and a quarter percent or so may not seem like a very good break-even point
examples.suggested: Ang tatlo at isang-kapat na porsyento o humigit-kumulang ay maaaring hindi mukhang napakagandang break-even point
examples.translation: Ang tatlo at isang-kapat na porsyento o thereabouts ay maaaring hindi mukhang napakagandang break-even point
examples.why: 'or so' is left as the untranslated English 'o thereabouts' — an ordinary English adverb, not a kept domain term, and a native technical writer would use 'humigit-kumulang'.

editor_note: Meaning is broadly faithful — the load-bearing physics survives intact (the caveat that "ang isang solong qubit ay hindi eksaktong katumbas ng isang boson o isang fermion", the A/B lattice cancellation argument with $(-1)^k$, the parity-mapping caveat that "ang interpretasyon ng isang qubit na naaayon sa isang orbital ay hindi naaangkop"), and core terms (qubit, Hamiltonian, ansatz, Pauli operator, ground state) are kept in English consistently. What a native technical editor would fix: several non-words / garbled verbs — "nasalipanan" (line 50, for "covered"), "iprinasimple" (line 52, where EN says *expressed* the cost function as a Hamiltonian, not simplified), "pinakamatipuno" (line 80, for "strongest"), "isalid" (line 130), "nagtatataboy" (line 125) — plus an untranslated adverb left mid-sentence ("maaari mong roughly isipin", line 184). Line 130 also drops the preposition, so "translate that **into** Pauli operators" becomes "isalin ang mga Pauli operator" (translate the Pauli operators), which is garbled rather than false but should be repaired. Person is also unstable within single paragraphs (namin/kami vs. natin/tayo, e.g. line 20 "binanggit namin … dumaan tayo … Binago namin") where EN uses one "we" throughout. None of these teaches a false concept, so MINOR rather than FAIL.

examples.source: Recall that, to map the max-cut problem, we expressed the cost function as a Hamiltonian using the QUBO formulation.
examples.suggested: … ipinahayag namin ang cost function bilang isang Hamiltonian gamit ang QUBO formulation.
examples.translation: Alalahanin na, upang i-map ang Max-Cut problem, iprinasimple namin ang cost function bilang isang Hamiltonian gamit ang QUBO formulation.
examples.why: "iprinasimple" (a malformed form of "pinasimple" = simplified) replaces "expressed"; QUBO re-expresses the cost function, it does not simplify it. Recoverable from context, so MINOR.

examples.source: Now once you have a general Hamiltonian, you are always going to want to translate that into Pauli operators, which are native to the quantum computer.
examples.suggested: … palagi mong gugustuhing isalin iyon tungo sa mga Pauli operator, na natural sa quantum computer.
examples.translation: Ngayon kapag mayroon ka nang pangkalahatang Hamiltonian, palagi mong gustong isalid ang mga Pauli operator, na natural sa quantum computer.
examples.why: "isalid" is not a Tagalog word (typo for "isalin"), and the missing "tungo sa/sa" turns "translate that into Pauli operators" into "translate the Pauli operators" — the direction of the conversion is lost.

examples.source: the one we have already covered in some depth: the max-cut example
examples.suggested: ang isa na natalakay na natin nang malalim: ang Max-Cut na halimbawa
examples.translation: ang isa na ating nasalipanan na nang malalalim: ang Max-Cut na halimbawa
examples.why: "nasalipanan" is not a Tagalog word; "malalalim" is also a stray plural. A native writer would use natalakay/nasaklaw.

examples.source: These interactions are strongest when the two amino acids are close to each other.
examples.suggested: … ay pinakamalakas kapag ang dalawang amino acid ay malapit sa isa't isa.
examples.translation: Ang mga pakikipag-ugnayang ito ay pinakamatipuno kapag ang dalawang amino acid ay malapit sa isa't isa.
examples.why: "matipuno" means sturdy/well-built (of a body), never used for interaction strength; the correct term is malakas.

examples.source: Instead, you can roughly think of the qubits as discretized pieces of space.
examples.suggested: Sa halip, maaari mong isipin nang halos ganito ang mga qubit: mga discretized na piraso ng espasyo.
examples.translation: Sa halip, maaari mong roughly isipin ang mga qubit bilang mga discretized na piraso ng espasyo.
examples.why: The English adverb "roughly" is left untranslated mid-clause, which no Tagalog technical writer would do; "halos" or "sa magaspang na paraan" is available.

examples.source: Here $a$ could take on any of the four possible directions.
examples.suggested: Dito ang $a$ ay maaaring magkaroon ng alinman sa apat na posibleng direksyon.
examples.translation: Dito ang $a$ ay maaaring mangailangan ng alinman sa apat na posibleng direksyon.
examples.why: "take on" is rendered as "mangailangan" (to require/need) instead of "to assume a value"; the index still clearly ranges over the four directions, so it is confusing rather than misleading.

examples.source: In Lesson 3 we discussed … we went through several steps … We transformed the problem …
examples.suggested: Use one consistent first-person plural (natin/tayo) throughout the paragraph.
examples.translation: Sa Lesson 3 tinalakay namin … dumaan tayo sa ilang mga hakbang … Binago namin ang problema …
examples.why: The exclusive "namin" and inclusive "tayo" alternate inside one paragraph where English has a single "we", which reads as inconsistent authorial voice in teaching prose.

editor_note: Nothing here teaches a false quantum-computing concept, but a native technical editor would fix several dropped/altered qualifiers and some calqued phrasing. Hedges are flattened: "not necessarily wrong" becomes the flat "Bagama't hindi ito mali", "fundamentally transform" becomes "panimulang baguhin" ("initially change" — panimula means beginning, not fundamental), "one day replace classical computers" becomes "palaging papalit" ("will always replace"), and "scientifically compelling" loses "scientifically" (and keeps "compelling" untranslated inside the clunky "theoretically na may pundasyon"). Terminology is otherwise correct and consistent (qubit, gate, circuit, Hamiltonian simulation, error correction/mitigation, variational, QPU all kept in English as the field does), and the register is correctly informal with no po/opo. Remaining slips are naturalness only: "Maaaring tawagan ito ng ilan na 'hype'" (tawagan = phone someone; should be tawagin), "hindi ka nito natakot mula sa kursong ito", "wala sa lahat ng mga bahaging ito", "nagbibigay-daan sa ito", "implicit na nag-ooperate", and "regimes" rendered as the geographic "rehiyon".

examples.source: While this is not necessarily wrong, it does not paint the full picture.
examples.suggested: Bagama't hindi naman ito basta-basta mali, hindi nito naipapakita ang buong larawan.
examples.translation: Bagama't hindi ito mali, hindi nito naibabahagi ang buong larawan.
examples.why: The English hedge "not necessarily" is dropped, turning a qualified concession into a flat endorsement of the misconception. Also "naibabahagi" (share) is an odd verb for "paint the picture".

examples.source: areas of active research that could fundamentally transform the way we approach important problems
examples.suggested: ...na maaaring lubusang baguhin ang paraan ng ating pagharap sa mahahalagang problema
examples.translation: mga lugar ng aktibong pananaliksik na maaaring panimulang baguhin ang paraan ng ating pagharap sa mahahalagang problema
examples.why: "Panimula" means beginning/initial, not fundamental; the claim is weakened from a deep transformation to a merely initial change.

examples.source: it is a common misconception that quantum computers will one day replace classical computers
examples.suggested: ...na balang-araw ay papalit ang mga quantum computer sa mga classical computer
examples.translation: isang karaniwang maling kaalaman na ang mga quantum computer ay palaging papalit sa mga classical computer
examples.why: "One day" (balang-araw) is rendered as "palaging" (always), restating the misconception being debunked as a different claim than the source's.

examples.source: Identifying specific regimes where quantum models might outperform classical ones
examples.suggested: Pagtukoy ng mga partikular na kondisyon/sitwasyon kung saan maaaring mahigitan ng mga quantum model ang mga classical na modelo
examples.translation: Pagtukoy ng mga partikular na rehiyon kung saan maaaring mahigitan ng mga quantum model ang mga classical
examples.why: "Rehiyon" in Tagalog reads as a geographic/administrative region; "regimes" here means parameter or problem settings, so the literal rendering points a learner at the wrong sense.

examples.source: One might even go so far as to call it "hype." / Hopefully that did not steer you away from this course / enabling it to serve as / a quantum computer does not have all these components / Quantum kernels that implicitly operate
examples.suggested: Mapapangahasan pa ngang tawagin ito ng ilan na "hype." / Sana hindi ka nito nailayo sa kursong ito / na nagbibigay-daan dito upang magsilbing / ang isang quantum computer ay walang lahat ng mga bahaging ito / ...na implisitong gumagana sa mga high-dimensional na feature space
examples.translation: Maaaring tawagan ito ng ilan na "hype." / Sana hindi ka nito natakot mula sa kursong ito / na nagbibigay-daan sa ito na magsilbing / ang isang quantum computer ay wala sa lahat ng mga bahaging ito / Mga quantum kernel na implicit na nag-ooperate
examples.why: Cluster of grammar/calque slips a native technical writer would not produce: tawagan (to phone) for tawagin, "natakot mula sa" calquing "steer away from", "sa ito" for dito, the ambiguous "wala sa lahat ng", and the Taglish "nag-ooperate".

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no drift, no hallucination; the tricky bits are all correct (max-TTL timer "не зупиняється та не призупиняється до його вичерпання", the reactivation caveat "Завдання має пройти через звичайну чергу", and the cost-limit qualifier "не буде доведено до кінця, якщо це перевищить ліміт витрат інстансу"), and the informal register (твої / вкажи / дивись) holds without a single Ви-slip. Three editor-level nits: "затримок через окреме постановлення кожного завдання в чергу" uses "постановлення" (a decree/resolution) where Ukrainian needs the verbal construction "через те, що кожне завдання доводиться окремо ставити в чергу"; "Користувачі плану Open Plan" is a tautology (plan-plan) — "Користувачі Open Plan" suffices; and "multi-job workload" is rendered two different ways in the same file — "експериментів із багатьма завданнями" in the batch section vs "багатозадачного робочого навантаження" (which reads as "multitasking") in the session section. None of these would mislead a learner.

examples.source: Using sessions helps avoid delays caused by queuing each job separately
examples.suggested: Використання сесій допомагає уникнути затримок, які виникають через те, що кожне завдання доводиться окремо ставити в чергу
examples.translation: Використання сесій допомагає уникнути затримок через окреме постановлення кожного завдання в чергу
examples.why: "постановлення" is a bureaucratic/legal noun (a decree); no Ukrainian technical writer would say "постановлення в чергу". The nominalized calque of the English gerund reads as MT.

examples.source: multi-job workloads / a multi-job workload
examples.suggested: use one rendering, e.g. "робоче навантаження з кількох завдань", in both sections
examples.translation: експериментів із багатьма завданнями (batch) … багатозадачного робочого навантаження (session)
examples.why: Same source concept split two ways within the file; "багатозадачний" additionally suggests multitasking rather than "made up of several jobs".

examples.source: Open Plan users cannot submit session jobs.
examples.suggested: Користувачі Open Plan не можуть подавати завдання в режимі сесії.
examples.translation: Користувачі плану Open Plan не можуть подавати завдання в режимі сесії.
examples.why: "плану Open Plan" repeats "plan" in both languages — a redundancy an editor would strike.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no drift, no hallucination: the location table ("Так"/"Так"), the single trigger case ("Коли змінюється стан завдання"), and all three field descriptions match the English one-for-one, and informal "ти/твоєму/дивись" holds everywhere. Two things a native editor would still change. (1) The appositive in the IBM Cloud Logs Routing sentence uses comma+em-dash on both sides ("[IBM Cloud Logs Routing,](…) — сервісом платформи, — щоб маршрутизувати…"), which is non-standard Ukrainian punctuation and reads clumsily; either commas or dashes, not both — and the trailing comma has been pulled inside the link text (same pattern on "About Logs Routing.", "IBM Cloud Logs.", "Fields that are included in platform logs."). (2) The same entity is called "сервісом платформи" in one paragraph and "службою IBM Cloud Logs Routing" in the next, an unnecessary сервіс/служба split within four lines. Neither misleads the learner.

examples.source: You can use IBM Cloud Logs Routing, which is a platform service, to route platform logs in your account to a destination of your choice…
examples.suggested: Ти можеш скористатися [IBM Cloud Logs Routing](…) — сервісом платформи — щоб маршрутизувати журнали платформи у своєму акаунті до обраного місця призначення…
examples.translation: Ти можеш скористатися [IBM Cloud Logs Routing,](…) — сервісом платформи, — щоб маршрутизувати журнали платформи у своєму акаунті до потрібного місця призначення…
examples.why: Mixing a comma and an em-dash on both sides of the apposition is non-standard Ukrainian punctuation, and the comma has been absorbed into the link text; a native technical writer would use dashes alone (or commas alone) and keep punctuation outside the link.

examples.source: …routed by IBM Cloud Logs Routing to an IBM Cloud Logs instance.
examples.suggested: …маршрутизуються сервісом IBM Cloud Logs Routing до екземпляра IBM Cloud Logs.
examples.translation: …маршрутизуються службою IBM Cloud Logs Routing до екземпляра IBM Cloud Logs.
examples.why: The preceding paragraph calls the very same product "сервісом платформи"; switching to "службою" four lines later is an avoidable within-file inconsistency for one term.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — the tricky "You will not be charged unless…" is correctly rendered with the Ukrainian double negative ("З тебе не стягуватиметься плата, якщо ти не створиш… і не використаєш…"), and the Pay-As-You-Go cost caveat plus the Open-plan escape hatch are both intact. Three editor-level slips: (1) a register/number break inside one sentence — "створи новий екземпляр і **призначте** його" mixes the informal "ти" imperative with the formal/plural "призначте" (should be "признач"); (2) the qualifier "instead" is dropped from "follow the steps in Install Qiskit instead", so the sentence no longer signals that this guide does not apply to that reader; (3) "щоб завершити наступне" is a calque of "to complete the following" — natural Ukrainian would be "щоб виконати наведене нижче". None of these misleads a learner.

examples.source: create a new instance and assign it to the Pay-As-You-Go Plan
examples.suggested: створи новий екземпляр і признач його до плану Pay-As-You-Go
examples.translation: створи новий екземпляр і призначте його до плану Pay-As-You-Go
examples.why: Formal/plural imperative 'призначте' collides with the informal 'ти' imperative 'створи' in the very same clause; the file is otherwise consistently 'ти' (виконай, пропусти, введи, спробуй).

examples.source: follow the steps in [Install Qiskit](/guides/install-qiskit) instead.
examples.suggested: натомість дотримуйся кроків у розділі [Встановлення Qiskit](/guides/install-qiskit).
examples.translation: дотримуйся кроків у розділі [Встановлення Qiskit](/guides/install-qiskit).
examples.why: 'instead' is dropped, so the contrast with the current guide (don't follow this one, follow that one) is lost; the reader could take it as an additional step rather than a redirect.

examples.source: follow the steps in the Set up to use IBM Cloud section to complete the following:
examples.suggested: виконай кроки з розділу ... щоб зробити таке / щоб виконати наведене нижче:
examples.translation: виконай кроки з розділу ... щоб завершити наступне:
examples.why: 'завершити наступне' is a double calque — 'наступне' for 'the following' is a Russianism/English calque in Ukrainian style guides, and 'завершити' (finish) is the wrong verb for tasks not yet started.
